        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>
        Print a completion script for a shell: bash, zsh, fish, elvish or
        powershell.

        Bash: podnet completions bash >
        ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/podnet. Zsh: podnet
        completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_podnet (with ~/.zfunc in fpath). Fish:
        podnet completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/podnet.fish.
        Elvish: podnet completions elvish > ~/.config/elvish/lib/podnet.elv,
        and use podnet in ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv. PowerShell: podnet
        completions powershell > ~/.config/powershell/podnet.ps1, and .
        ~/.config/powershell/podnet.ps1 in $PROFILE.

        <SHELL>
            Values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh. Required.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet update [OPTIONS]
        Replace this binary with the binary of a release, after checking its
        signature (cosign, release.yml at the tag) and its SHA-256

        --check
            Only say which release is available; change nothing

        --rollback
            Put the binary before the last update (podnet.prev) back, with no
            network. A second --rollback goes forward again

        --force
            Install the release also when it is the version of this binary.
            Without it, podnet says that the version is installed and exits 0

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Say whether a newer release exists. podnet update installs it after it
        checks the cosign signature and the SHA-256.
            $ podnet update --check

    podnet qr [OPTIONS] <URL>

        <URL>

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with

            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet demo [OPTIONS]
        Test the full path: a built-in origin, a tunnel, a fetch of the URL

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --exit-on-verify
            Exit as soon as the public URL has been fetched

        --token <TOKEN>
            Named-tunnel token. Prefer the variable TUNNEL_TOKEN or
            --token-file: other users of the host can read a command line.
            Variable: TUNNEL_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the named-tunnel token from this file (for example a secret
            of a container). The token is not on the command line. Variable:
            TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Make a quick tunnel to the built-in origin, and fetch its public URL.
            $ podnet demo --exit-on-verify

    podnet net shim [OPTIONS]

        --out <OUT>

            web=10.66.0.2

        --map-file <PATH>

        --socks-route <ROUTE>

        --json

    podnet net proxy [OPTIONS]
        Run a SOCKS5 / HTTP CONNECT proxy into the virtual network

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --listen <LISTEN>
            Where to accept proxy clients: unix:/path or tcp://[bind:]port.
            Default: unix:/tmp/podnet-vnet.socks.

        --map <NAME=ADDR>
            Name-to-address entries, repeatable: --map web=10.66.0.2

        --map-file <PATH>
            Read name entries from a file, repeatable: `NAME=ADDR` or hosts
            lines. The names answer at the gateway 10.66.0.1:53 and at the
            proxy

        --forward <VIRT=REAL>
            Forward a virtual endpoint to a real one, repeatable. REAL is
            host:port (a name or an address) for TCP, or unix:/path for a unix
            service. A target that is not loopback goes through the proxy of
            the process (with NO_PROXY); a loopback target and a unix path go
            direct: --forward 10.66.0.2:8080=127.0.0.1:3000

        --port <PORT>
            Port to use when a client omits one. Default: 80.

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C

        --switch <SWITCH>
            Connect the stack to a switch (unix:/path or tcp://host:port)
            instead of a loopback link, so it reaches stacks on other hosts

        --switch-token-file <PATH>
            With a TCP --switch: read the shared token of the switch from this
            file. Without it, the token is the variable PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN

        --address <ADDRESS>
            The IPv4 address of this stack on the switch, for example
            10.66.0.3

        --drop <DROP>
            With --switch: drop this part of the packets that this stack sends
            to the switch (0.0 to 1.0), for tests. Default: 0.

        --duplicate <DUPLICATE>
            With --switch: send this part of the packets two times (0.0 to
            1.0), for tests. Default: 0.

        --reorder <REORDER>
            With --switch: send this part of the packets out of order (0.0 to
            1.0), for tests. Default: 0.

        --seed <SEED>
            With --switch: the seed of the fault sequence. Default: 1.

        --control <CONTROL>
            With --switch: serve the shim control socket with this abstract
            name. A shim program with PODNET_VNET_CONTROL=NAME that binds a
            virtual address can then accept connections from other hosts

        --import <VIRT>
            With --switch: make a remote virtual address reachable for shim
            programs on this host, repeatable: --import 10.66.0.3:8080

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        A virtual address for a real service.
            $ podnet net proxy --forward 10.66.0.2:8080=unix:/run/app.sock

    podnet net switch [OPTIONS]
        Run a switch that connects stacks on this host and on other hosts

        --listen <LISTEN>
            Where to accept stacks: unix:/path or tcp://host:port. A TCP
            listener needs a shared token (PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN or
            --switch-token-file); a unix listener takes the same user only.
            Default: unix:/tmp/podnet-vnet.switch.

        --switch-token-file <PATH>
            With a TCP --listen: read the shared token from this file. Without
            it, the token is the variable PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN. Each TCP peer
            must send it

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        A switch on TCP. Each stack gives the same token: --switch-token-file,
        or PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN.
            $ podnet net switch --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:7000
            --switch-token-file /run/secrets/switch

    podnet net tailscale [OPTIONS]
        Run a SOCKS5 / HTTP CONNECT front door to a tailnet through tailscaled

        --socket <SOCKET>
            The LocalAPI socket of tailscaled. Default:
            /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock.

        --listen <LISTEN>
            Where to accept proxy clients: unix:/path or tcp://[bind:]port. A
            unix path that another process serves exits 69; a file that is not
            a socket exits 64; a stale socket is removed. Default:
            unix:/tmp/podnet-socks.sock.

        --port <PORT>
            Port to use when a client omits one. Default: 80.

        --tailnet <NAME>
            The tailnet that the daemon must run in (its name or its DNS
            suffix). The door starts only when tailscaled is Running in it
            (exit 78 for another tailnet, 69 after 20 s with no login). Then
            new dials are refused while the daemon is in another tailnet. Also
            the variable PODNET_TAILNET. A host that reaches only port 443
            starts tailscaled with TS_FORCE_NOISE_443=true

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet net socksify [OPTIONS]
        Build the LD_PRELOAD shim that sends tailnet connects to a front door

        --out <OUT>
            Directory to write and compile the shim into

        --socket <PATH>
            The unix socket of the front door (exported as
            PODNET_SOCKS_PROXY). It is not --proxy: that is the global proxy
            URL of podnet. Default: /tmp/podnet-socks.sock.

        --cidr <ROUTE>
            Route only these destinations, repeatable (exported as
            PODNET_SOCKS_CIDRS): tailnet, ADDR, ADDR/BITS, IPV4:PORT or
            [IPV6]:PORT. With no --cidr, the shim routes the tailnet only
            (100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48). Example: --cidr
            127.0.0.1:3000

        --log
            Log each route and each redirect to stderr

        --json
            Print the environment as JSON instead of shell assignments

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet net passwd-shim [OPTIONS]
        Write a passwd file and the fakepwd preload for a client (ssh,
        ssh-keygen, git) on a host with no /etc/passwd entry for this user.
        Then ssh-keygen writes its key (with no shim it exits 0 and writes no
        key). Use: eval "$(podnet net passwd-shim)"

        --out <OUT>
            Directory for passwd, group, getent, id and fakepwd.so. It must
            belong to this user, and other users must not write it. Default:
            `podnet-ts-shims` in the first private directory that is not
            noexec (as for `net shim`)

        --user <USER>
            Local login name. Default: the current user

        --uid <UID>
            Local uid. Default: the current uid

        --gid <GID>
            Local gid. Default: the current gid

        --shell <SHELL>
            Login shell of the synthetic user

        --json
            Print the client environment as JSON

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Cloudflare WARP client: registration, account, proxy, run

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet warp: register, status, license, rotate, delete,
        probe, exit, export, scan, forward, proxy, up, down, env, exec, shell,
        nc, ssh-config, tun, run.

    podnet warp register [OPTIONS]
        Register a device (or load the saved one) and print it

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp status [OPTIONS]
        Print the device and the account (type, WARP+ state, quota)

        --json
            Print the account record as JSON

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

    podnet warp license [OPTIONS] <KEY>
        Attach a WARP+ license key to the device

        <KEY>

    podnet warp rotate [OPTIONS]
        Make a new MASQUE key and enrol it. The old key stops working

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp delete [OPTIONS]
        Remove the device from the WARP service and delete the saved file

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp probe [OPTIONS]
        Open the tunnel and test TCP connects through it. Exit 69 when a
        target fails

        --target <TARGET>
            A TCP destination to reach through the tunnel, host:port

        --identity <PATH>

    podnet warp exit [OPTIONS]
        Open the tunnel and print its exit: the data center (colo), the
        country and the address that a destination sees (from
        http://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace), and the IPv6 egress address (the trace
        at 2606:4700:4700::1111, else the TXT of whoami.cloudflare). Exit 69
        when there is no answer

        --json
            Print one JSON object

        --no-ipv6
            Do not ask for the IPv6 egress address

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral

    podnet warp export [OPTIONS]
        Print a WireGuard config of a new WARP device (wg-quick or JSON), for
        other clients. The device and its private key are in warp-wg.json of
        the state directory, not in warp.json. Its data path is WireGuard on
        UDP (port 2408), not MASQUE on TCP 443. The output holds the private
        key: a terminal is refused with no --out (--out - prints it), and a
        redirected file becomes mode 0600. WARP reads 3 reserved bytes in each
        message; kernel WireGuard and wg-quick send zeros. --check tells if
        the device needs the bytes

        --format <FORMAT>
            wg-quick or json. Default: wg-quick. Values: wg-quick, json.

        --out <FILE>
            Write the config to this file (mode 0600) in place of stdout

        --export-identity <FILE>
            The file of the exported device (default: warp-wg.json in the
            state directory)

        --endpoint <HOST:PORT>
            The Endpoint of the config, HOST:PORT (default: the endpoint of
            the device record, port 2408)

        --keepalive <SECS>
            PersistentKeepalive in seconds; 0 writes no line. Default: 25.

        --new
            Register a new device even when the file has one

        --delete
            Remove the exported device from the service and delete its file

        --check
            Test the data path of the device and write no config: the
            WireGuard leg of podnet with the reserved bytes, then with zeros
            (as kernel WireGuard and wg-quick send), each with a TCP connect
            to the target of --probe (default 1.1.1.1:443). Prints "device ok"
            (exit 0), "needs reserved bytes" (exit 1) or "device data path
            dead, use --new" (exit 69)

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).

            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:

            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp scan [OPTIONS]
        Measure front doors of WARP: the TCP connect and the TLS handshake
        with the pinned key, for each --candidate and the front doors of the
        device record. The fastest goes first. Exit 69 when none answers

        --candidate <IP[:PORT]>
            A front door to measure: IP or IP:PORT (port 443); an IPv6 address
            with a port is in brackets. Repeatable

        --timeout-ms <MS>
            The time limit of each front door, in milliseconds (100 to 60000).
            Default: 3000.

        --json
            Print one JSON document

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp forward [OPTIONS]
        Forward local listeners through WARP (as ssh -L): each connection to
        LISTEN goes through the tunnel to HOST:PORT

        -L, --local <LISTEN=HOST:PORT>
            LISTEN=HOST:PORT. LISTEN is PORT (on 127.0.0.1), ADDR:PORT,
            tcp://ADDR:PORT or unix:/PATH. HOST is resolved inside the tunnel;
            a tunnel: prefix is accepted. Repeatable. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FORWARD.

        --list
            Print the forwards of the detached instances (podnet ps) and exit

        --strict
            Exit 69 when any listener does not start

        --max-connections <N>
            The most connections of each listener at the same time. 0: no
            limit. Default: 32.

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,

            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:

            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
