        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet link [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        A link between two installs over a carrier (a unix socket, memory):
        each end proves its Ed25519 key, and an allow list (default deny) says
        which peers may open streams. Listen, dial, status, close, carriers

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet link: listen, dial, connect, status, close,
        carriers.

    podnet link listen [OPTIONS] --allow <FILE> <ADDRESS>
        Listen at an address of a carrier. A peer must prove its key, and the
        allow list (--allow) must hold it, before it can open a stream. Print
        the address (for the unix carrier: the path and its mode 0600) and the
        fingerprint of this install. Each stream of an admitted peer goes to
        --to. A second listener at a live address exits 69; a peer that the
        list does not hold exits 77 at its side

        <ADDRESS>
            The address, in the form of the carrier: a path for `unix`, a name
            for `memory`. Required.

        --carrier <NAME>
            The carrier (`podnet link carriers` lists them). Default: unix.

        --allow-other-uid
            The unix carrier accepts a peer of another uid. Each end checks
            the uid of the other end (SO_PEERCRED), so give the flag at both
            ends. Without it, a peer of another uid is refused (exit 69)

        --ring <BYTES>
            The bytes of each ring of the memory carrier: 65536 to 67108864
            (64 KiB to 64 MiB). Default 1048576

        --allow <FILE>
            The allow list: a file with one peer on each line (the fingerprint
            that `podnet link status` shows, a `SHA256:` fingerprint, or a key
            in hex), 4096 lines at most. The list is default deny: a peer that
            it does not hold gets exit 77. The file must not be writable by
            others (else exit 71); a missing file exits 66. Required.

        --to <TARGET>
            Where the streams of the service `raw` go: `host:port` or
            `unix:/path`. It is the same as `--service raw=TARGET`. Without a
            service, the listener refuses each stream (the opener exits 69)

        --service <NAME=TARGET>
            A service of this listener: NAME=TARGET, with a NAME of 1 to 32
            characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - and a TARGET as in --to. A peer
            reaches it with `link dial --service NAME` or
            `peer:FINGERPRINT/NAME`. Repeat it: 16 services at most

        --control <PATH>
            The control socket (mode 0600, with the token file PATH.token).
            The default is `link-PID.ctl` in the run directory of podnet. The
            ready document names it. `podnet link status` reads it

        --json
            Print the ready document as one line of JSON in place of the text

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        A link listener on a unix socket (mode 0600). A peer must prove its
        key and be in peers.txt.
            $ podnet link listen /run/user/1000/app.sock --allow peers.txt
            --to unix:/run/user/1000/origin.sock --detach

    podnet link dial [OPTIONS] <ADDRESS>
        Connect to a listener, prove this key, and check the key of the
        listener against --peer or --allow. Then copy stdin and stdout over
        one stream. A listener that is not allowed exits 77

        <ADDRESS>
            The address of the listener, in the form of the carrier. Required.

        --carrier <NAME>
            The carrier (`podnet link carriers` lists them). Default: unix.

        --allow-other-uid
            The unix carrier accepts a peer of another uid. Each end checks
            the uid of the other end (SO_PEERCRED), so give the flag at both
            ends. Without it, a peer of another uid is refused (exit 69)

        --ring <BYTES>
            The bytes of each ring of the memory carrier: 65536 to 67108864
            (64 KiB to 64 MiB). Default 1048576

        --peer <FINGERPRINT>
            The fingerprint that the listener must prove (the line that its
            `podnet link listen` prints). Repeat it for more than one

        --allow <FILE>
            An allow list file, as `link listen --allow`, of the listeners
            that this install trusts. Give --peer or --allow: the list is
            default deny, and a listener that it does not hold exits 77

        --service <NAME>
            The service to ask the listener for (`link listen --service`). A
            name of 1 to 32 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. A listener with
            no such service, or whose origin does not answer, exits 69.
            Default: raw.

        --check
            Connect and check the peer, print its fingerprint, and exit 0. It
            opens no stream

        --json
            With --check: print one JSON document

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Connect to a link listener, check its key, and print its fingerprint.
            $ podnet link dial /run/user/1000/app.sock --peer FINGERPRINT
            --check

    podnet link connect [OPTIONS] <ADDRESS>
        Connect to a listener, prove this key, check the key of the listener
        against --peer or --allow, and hold the link. Other programs open
        streams of the link through its control socket: `peer:FINGERPRINT/
        SERVICE` as a network (podnet forward -L LISTEN=peer:FINGERPRINT/
        SERVICE). The command ends when the link ends (exit 69) or at a stop
        signal

        <ADDRESS>
            The address of the listener, in the form of the carrier. Required.

        --carrier <NAME>
            The carrier (`podnet link carriers` lists them). Default: unix.

        --allow-other-uid
            The unix carrier accepts a peer of another uid. Each end checks
            the uid of the other end (SO_PEERCRED), so give the flag at both
            ends. Without it, a peer of another uid is refused (exit 69)

        --ring <BYTES>
            The bytes of each ring of the memory carrier: 65536 to 67108864
            (64 KiB to 64 MiB). Default 1048576

        --peer <FINGERPRINT>
            The fingerprint that the listener must prove (the line that its
            `podnet link listen` prints). Repeat it for more than one

        --allow <FILE>
            An allow list file, as `link listen --allow`, of the listeners
            that this install trusts. Give --peer or --allow (else exit 64); a
            listener that the list does not hold exits 77

        --control <PATH>
            The control socket (mode 0600, with the token file PATH.token).
            The default is `link-PID.ctl` in the run directory of podnet. The
            ready document names it

        --json
            Print the ready document as one line of JSON in place of the text

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Hold a link to a listener and run a control socket for it.
            $ podnet link connect /run/user/1000/app.sock --peer FINGERPRINT
            --control /run/user/1000/link.ctl --detach --name peer1

    podnet link status [OPTIONS] [NAME]
        Show the fingerprint of this install and the link instances that run
        (podnet ps lists the other instances). With a NAME, show that instance
        only. For an instance with a control socket, status asks the socket
        for the links it holds (peer, streams, counters) and shows them under
        `live`; if the socket does not answer, status shows the record

        <NAME>
            The name of a link instance (podnet ps). Default: each one

        --create
            Make the key of this install when there is none (mode 0600 in the
            state directory). Without it, status writes nothing

        --json
            Print one JSON document

        --control <PATH>
            Ask this control socket only (the `control` of the ready document
            of an instance). A wrong token exits 77, and a socket that does
            not answer exits 69

        --token-file <FILE>
            The token file of --control. Default: PATH.token

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet link close [OPTIONS] <NAME>
        Stop a link instance that runs in the background. First end each link
        of the instance through its control socket (the verb close-link), so
        that the peers get a GOAWAY; then SIGTERM, and SIGKILL after
        --timeout. The listener removes its unix socket

        <NAME>
            The name of the link instance (podnet link status). Required.

        --timeout <TIMEOUT>
            Seconds to wait before SIGKILL. Default: 10.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet link carriers [OPTIONS]
        List the carriers of this build, with the flags of each and whether
        this host can use it. A carrier that this host cannot use gives its
        reason

        --carrier <NAME>
            The carrier (`podnet link carriers` lists them). Default: unix.

        --allow-other-uid
            The unix carrier accepts a peer of another uid. Each end checks
            the uid of the other end (SO_PEERCRED), so give the flag at both
            ends. Without it, a peer of another uid is refused (exit 69)

        --ring <BYTES>
            The bytes of each ring of the memory carrier: 65536 to 67108864
            (64 KiB to 64 MiB). Default 1048576

        --json
            Print one JSON document: {"carriers": [...]}

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:

        --no-proxy

        --egress <SPEC>

            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet pod [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...
        Run a program with all its traffic sent through a proxy
        (podnet-netns).

        Give the podnet-netns arguments after `pod`. See `podnet pod --help`.
        podnet gives the line after `pod` to podnet-netns: the global options
        of podnet (-q, -v, --color, --log-format) do not apply to it.

        Run a program with all egress through a proxy, without shims

        Usage: podnet pod [OPTIONS] -- <PROGRAM> [ARGS]...
               podnet pod doctor [--json]
               podnet pod --serve <LISTEN> -x <PROXY>

        Arguments:
          <PROGRAM> [ARGS]... The program to run, and its arguments

        Options:
          -x, --proxy <SPEC> Upstream proxy, repeatable; more than one chains:
                                     socks5://[user:pass@]host:port
                                     http://[user:pass@]host:port
                                     socks5://unix:/path (unix-socket proxy)
                                     http://unix:/path (HTTP CONNECT on a unix
                                     socket)
                                     socks5h+unix:/path, http+unix:/path (the
                                     same)
                                     tailscale:/path/to/tailscaled.sock
                                   Default: $ALL_PROXY, $HTTPS_PROXY or
                                   $HTTP_PROXY.
                                   --egress SPEC is the same option (its name
                                   in each
                                   podnet command)
          -r, --rule <SPEC> Per-destination route; first match wins:
                                     domain:NAME=socks5://host:port
                                     domain:.example.com=... (the name and
                                     each
                                                               name under it)
                                     cidr:10.0.0.0/8=socks5://host:port
                                     cidr:10.0.0.0/8=direct (no proxy)
                                     domain:.ads.example=reject (refuse; also
                                     block):
                                     connect fails with ECONNREFUSED (netns: a
                                     RST),
                                     a datagram with EACCES (netns: dropped),
                                     --serve answers SOCKS5 0x02 or HTTP 403
                                   With the seccomp backend, 127.0.0.0/8 goes
                                   direct
                                   (or to a listener of the program itself)
              --allow-shadowed-rules
                                   A rule that an earlier rule shadows (it can
                                   never
                                   match) gives a warning. A shadowed reject
                                   rule is
                                   an error (exit 64); this option makes it a
                                   warning
              --default-action <A> allow (default) or reject: what the pod
              does with a
                                   target that no rule matches. reject refuses
                                   it as
                                   a reject rule does
              --loopback-rules Seccomp backend: apply the rules to a TCP
              connect to
                                   127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 (by default it goes
                                   direct). A
                                   refused one gets ECONNREFUSED; an allowed
                                   one goes
                                   direct
              --flow-log <FILE> Append one JSON line to FILE for each decision
                                   (time, target, rule or default, chain,
                                   verdict)
                                   and one at the close of each relayed TCP
                                   flow
                                   (bytes_out, bytes_in)
              --learn <FILE> Write each destination of the run to FILE, one
                                   PROTO TARGET line each. A flow that a rule
                                   refuses goes through the -x chain
              --fail-on-violation <FILE>
                                   Refuse each destination that is not in FILE
                                   (a
                                   file of --learn). A learned destination
                                   that a
                                   rule refuses is also a violation. The pod
                                   writes
                                   each violation on stderr and exits 4 when
                                   the
                                   program exits 0
              --flow-budget <N> Seccomp backend: the most sockets of the
              program
                                   that the pod tracks at one time (64 to
                                   1048576).
                                   A socket call above it gets EMFILE.
                                   Default: from
                                   RLIMIT_NOFILE (pod doctor shows it)
              --map <NAME=ADDR> Resolve NAME to ADDR locally, repeatable
              --keep-proxy-env Keep HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and
              NO_PROXY
                                   (and the lower-case forms) for the program;
                                   by
                                   default the program does not get them
              --backend <NAME> auto (default), netns or seccomp. With netns, a
                                   listener of the program is in the network
                                   of the
                                   pod: a loopback TCP listener is not seen
                                   from
                                   outside; use a unix socket (connect -L
                                   unix:///PATH)
              --prefer-udp With auto: seccomp first when it works (UDP
                                   datagrams of any size go through; netns
                                   carries
                                   a datagram of 1500 bytes at most)
              --name-backend Print one line on stderr that names the backend
                                   that runs, its limits and the reason of the
                                   choice (also after auto)
              --inbound-dir <DIR> Where a bound port is exposed as a unix
              socket
                                   (seccomp backend only). The directory must
                                   be of
                                   this user and not writable by the group or
                                   by
                                   others; a new one gets mode 0700
                                   [default:
                                   $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet-netns-inbound,
                                   else $TMPDIR/podnet-netns-inbound-UID]
              --host-gateway Netns backend: a TCP connect to the gateway of
              the
                                   pod (10.66.255.254) and a port goes to
                                   127.0.0.1
                                   and that port on the host; a UDP datagram
                                   to the
                                   gateway (not port 53) goes from a UDP
                                   socket of
                                   the host. Off by default: the connect is
                                   refused
              --session <DIR> Seccomp backend: share the inbound listeners
                                   (DIR/inbound, unless --inbound-dir) and the
                                   fake
                                   DNS table (DIR/dns) with each pod of DIR.
                                   The
                                   directory must be of this user and not
                                   writable
                                   by the group or by others. The netns
                                   backend does
                                   not use it
              --serve <LISTEN> Serve SOCKS5, HTTP CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE on
                                   unix:/path or tcp://host:port, forwarding
                                   through
                                   the -x chain. At most 1024 live clients; a
                                   plain
                                   http:// request gets 405 and BIND gets 0x07
              --early-reply With --serve: answer a CONNECT that the rules take
                                   before the dial, hold the first 64 KiB of
                                   the
                                   client, and send the SOCKS5 greeting and
                                   request
                                   to the upstream in one write. A failed dial
                                   then
                                   closes the connection: the client gets no
                                   error
                                   code. The flow log has a refused line. Off
                                   by
                                   default
          -v, --verbose Log each flow; with seccomp, also each socket and
                                   each setsockopt that the pod emulates
          -V, --version Print the version
          -h, --help Print help

        Exit status: the exit code of the program; 64 for a usage mistake
        (also no
        proxy at all); 3 when no backend can run on this host; 4 for a
        violation of
        --fail-on-violation when the program exits 0. The pod returns when
        the program exits; a process that the program started keeps the
        network of
        the pod until it exits. doctor measures what
        the host permits and exits 3 when no backend can run.


        <ARGS>...
            The podnet-netns arguments

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Run a program with all its traffic through a proxy.
            $ podnet pod -x socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 -- curl
            https://example.com

    podnet man [OPTIONS] [SECTION]...
        Show the manual, generated from this binary

        <SECTION>...
            Sections: commands (tunnel, warp run) and topics (environment,
            files, exit-status, examples, pod). `podnet man tunnel serve`
            gives both

        --no-pager
            Write to stdout, also on a terminal

        --roff
            Write a man(7) page

        --json
            Write the manual as one JSON object

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --resolve <HOST=IP>

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        This manual as a man(7) page.
            $ podnet man --roff

    podnet status [OPTIONS]
        Print one line of JSON about this host. It opens no connection

        --json

        --color <COLOR>

        Examples:

    podnet doctor [OPTIONS]
        Test the path from this host to the edge: the proxy, TCP and TLS to
        the APIs, the edge (7844) and MASQUE (443), and UDP 7844. Exit 0 when
        at least one leg (quic, http2, quic+warp) can work, 1 when none can

        --json
            Print one JSON document

        --quick
            A short run: one sample for each path, and 15 s for the whole run.
            A part that does not end in time gets the verdict `unknown`. The
            JSON document keeps the same keys

        --agent
            Test what dev work can do here: git over HTTPS and SSH, the
            package registries, UDP DNS, IPv6 and localhost, directly, through
            the proxy and through a running podnet warp up; then print the
            commands to run

        --samples <SAMPLES>
            Samples of each TCP path (1-9). All samples end in 10 s. Default:
            9.

        --timeout <TIMEOUT>
            The time limit of one connection and of one TLS handshake, in
            seconds. Default: 3.

        --relay <URL>
            The relay to test, as the `--relay` of `tunnel` (a loopback
            `http://` relay is allowed). Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ssh-relay <HOST:PORT>
            Also test the SSH relay of `podnet ssh-relay`: the TCP connect,
            the SSH banner and the auth with --ssh-user, with no session.
            Default: the relay of a running `ssh-relay` instance; else the row
            is `unknown`

        --ssh-user <USER>
            The SSH user of --ssh-relay

        --connect-proxy <HOST:PORT>
            The HTTP CONNECT proxy of --ssh-relay: HOST:PORT. It replaces the
            proxy of the process (--proxy, PODNET_PROXY, the proxy variables).
            Default: that proxy, if it is an HTTP proxy with no credentials;
            else the row says why it does not dial

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Test the path from this host to the edge; the last line names the step
        to take.
            $ podnet doctor

    podnet autostart [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Start a podnet command at boot, with no root: a systemd user unit (it
        stops at logout unless linger is on), else an @reboot line in the
        crontab

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>

            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand

            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY

            PODNET_PROXY.

        --egress <SPEC>

            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the

            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet autostart: add, remove, list, run.

    podnet autostart add [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <ARGS>...]
        Add an entry that runs `podnet ARGS`. The token and a proxy password
        go to a private env file (mode 0600), not to the unit, the crontab or
        the command line. Exit 69 when this host has no systemd user manager
        and no crontab

        <NAME>
            The name of the entry (letters, digits, - and _). Required.

        <ARGS>...
            The podnet command and its arguments, after `--`, with no leading
            `podnet` (one is dropped). The command must parse

        --from <INSTANCE>
            Take the command and its arguments from the detached instance
            INSTANCE (podnet ps), with no --detach options

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet autostart run [OPTIONS] --dir <DIR> <NAME>
        Run an entry in the place of this process: the unit and the crontab
        line call this. It reads NAME.args and NAME.env in DIR

        <NAME>
            The name of the entry. Required.

        --dir <DIR>
            The directory of the entries (`<state>/autostart`). Required.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand

            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --egress <SPEC>

            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH, netbird:[PORT] and
            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        One command for a sandbox with basic networking: test what works,
        start WARP when it is needed, expose ports, and print what works now
        and the commands to use

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the

            PODNET_PROXY.

        --egress <SPEC>

            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet agent: up, down, status.

    podnet agent up [OPTIONS]
        Test the host (podnet doctor --agent), start podnet warp up when
        direct networking does not do each task, start a detached quick tunnel
        for each --expose PORT, and print one JSON document

        --persist
            Also add the block of podnet warp up --persist to the shell files

        --expose <PORT>
            A local port to expose with a quick tunnel (repeatable)

        --port <PORT>
            The TCP port of the WARP proxy on 127.0.0.1. Default: 40000.

        --warp
            Start WARP also when direct networking works

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand

            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.

            PODNET_PROXY.

            unix:/PATH). wg:FILE is for podnet forward --network and podnet
            route

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        In a sandbox: test what works, start WARP when it is needed, and print
        the commands to use.
            $ podnet agent up

        Examples:
