```text
ENVIRONMENT
    HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, ALL_PROXY, all_proxy
        The proxy for each connection of podnet, when --proxy and --no-proxy
        are not given: http://, socks5:// (this host resolves the name) or
        socks5h:// (the proxy resolves it), [user:password@]host[:port]. The
        first variable that is set and can be parsed is used. With a proxy,
        --protocol auto does not try QUIC on UDP 7844. podnet pod uses the
        value as its default upstream. (tunnel, warp, edge discovery, pod)
    NO_PROXY, no_proxy
        The targets that do not use the proxy, separated by commas: * (all), a
        name (it matches the names under it too), .name, an IP address, a
        network (10.0.0.0/8), each with an optional :port. (all commands)
    PODNET_RESOLVE
        Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP]. --resolve
        adds to it. Without a pin, podnet asks the system resolver, then DNS
        over HTTPS at 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4. A bad value is a
        configuration error (exit 78) for each command. (all commands)
    PODNET_TAILNET
        The tailnet that tailscaled must run in, in place of --tailnet: the
        name or the DNS suffix. The door starts only when the daemon is
        Running in it, and refuses new dials when the daemon changes to
        another tailnet. (net tailscale)
    TS_FORCE_NOISE_443
        Read only, to show its value in the tailscaled row of net doctor. It
        is a variable of tailscaled: set it to true when tailscaled starts on
        a host that reaches only port 443 (the control connection tries port
        80 first). (net doctor)
    NB_SOCKS5_LISTENER_PORT
        Read only, to find the SOCKS5 listener of NetBird netstack mode in the
        NetBird row of net doctor (default 1080). It is a variable of the
        NetBird daemon. The network spec netbird:[PORT] gives its own port.
        (net doctor)
    HTTP_PROXY, http_proxy
        The default upstream of podnet pod when HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY are
        not set. (pod)
    TUNNEL_TOKEN
        The named-tunnel token, in place of --token. Other users of the host
        can read a command line, but not the environment of a process of
        another user. (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE
        A file with the named-tunnel token, in place of --token-file.
        TUNNEL_TOKEN wins when both are set. An empty file is a usage error
        (exit 64). (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    SSL_CERT_FILE
        The only file of TLS roots (PEM), when --ca-file is not given. Without
        both, podnet trusts podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the first system
        bundle that it can read, and the roots compiled into podnet. (all
        commands)
    PODNET_STATE_DIR
        The state directory (the WARP identity). The value none keeps no file.
        Without it, podnet takes the first directory that it can write of
        $XDG_STATE_HOME/podnet, $HOME/.local/state/podnet,
        $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet and podnet-<uid> in the temporary directory.
        On a host whose home is on a shared disk, set it to a directory of
        this host, so that two hosts do not share one WARP device. (warp,
        tunnel --transport warp)
    PODNET_WARP_SOCKET
        The socket of the running podnet warp up; podnet warp up sets it in
        its env file and for the program of warp exec. These commands try
        --socket, else this variable, then warp.sock in the run directory,
        then the socket of the pointer file that podnet warp up writes
        ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/warp-up.json, else podnet-<uid>/warp-up.json
        in the temporary directory; mode 0600). So they find a podnet warp up
        that has another state directory. (warp exec, warp shell, warp nc,
        agent)
    XDG_STATE_HOME, HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, TMPDIR
        The candidates of the state directory, and of the directory of a shim
        (a directory that is not noexec). podnet reads the home from HOME
        only, not from the user database. (warp, net shim, net socksify,
        autostart)
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME
        The base of the systemd user unit:
        $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user/podnet-NAME.service, else
        $HOME/.config/systemd/user. (autostart)
    PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER
        The value of --leg-failover when the flag is not given: staggered or
        serial. (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    NO_COLOR
        When set, the log has no colours. The log has colours only when stderr
        is a terminal. (all commands)
    PODNET_EDGE
        A comma-separated list of ip:port edge addresses. It replaces edge
        discovery. A value that cannot be parsed is a configuration error
        (exit 78). (tunnel, serve, share, demo, doctor, net doctor)
    PODNET_PROXY
        The value of --proxy when the flag is not given: http://, socks5:// or
        socks5h://HOST:PORT, SCHEME+unix:/PATH, or SCHEME+exec:COMMAND (a
        proxy at the stdin and stdout of a command). It keeps a proxy password
        out of the command line; podnet autostart puts it in the private env
        file of an entry. The env file of podnet warp up with no TCP listener
        sets it to the unix socket. (all commands)
    PODNET_WARP_SHELL
        Set in a shell that podnet warp shell started; the block of --persist
        then does not start it again. (warp shell, the block of warp up
        --persist)
    SHELL
        The shell that podnet warp shell runs (default /bin/sh). (warp shell)
    PODNET_RUN_DIR
        The directory of the detached instances (mode 0700): NAME.json,
        NAME.lock and NAME.log for each, and NAME.secrets (mode 0600) for an
        instance with a token or a proxy password. Default:
        $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/run, else run in the state directory.
        (--detach, ps, stop, logs, wait)
    PODNET_LINK_CONTROL
        The control socket of the link instance that holds the link to the
        peer (the control of the ready document of podnet link connect or
        listen). Its token is in PATH.token. Without it, podnet asks the
        control socket of each link instance in the run directory. (forward,
        any command with a peer:FINGERPRINT/SERVICE network)
    PODNET_DETACH_NAME, PODNET_DETACH_HASH, PODNET_DETACH_COMMAND,
    PODNET_DETACH_SUPERVISED, PODNET_DETACH_READY_TIMEOUT
        podnet sets them for the child of --detach: the name of the instance,
        the hash of its arguments, the command, whether a supervisor runs it,
        and the --ready-timeout of the first start (a provision of a quick
        tunnel does not wait past it). Do not set them. (--detach)
    PODNET_RELAY
        The value of --relay when the flag is not given: the WebSocket-to-TCP
        relay of --transport relay (https:// and a host), or a comma list of
        hosts of one deployment. The default is
        https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev; when a host does not answer, podnet
        tries hosts of its pool. (tunnel, serve, share, demo, relay)
    PODNET_REPO
        OWNER/NAME of the releases for scripts/install.sh. podnet update does
        not use it: its repository names the signer of the binary. A warning
        says so. (update)
    PODNET_FOREIGN_HOME
        allow: write in a directory of another user anyway (with a warning).
        By default, podnet writes no file in a directory that belongs to
        another user (root with the HOME of a user): the state directory skips
        that HOME, and the other commands exit 78. (the state directory, warp
        ssh-config --write, warp up --persist and --env-d, autostart)
    PODNET_AUTH_USER, PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE
        The values of --auth-user and --auth-password-file: each visitor of
        the tunnel must give this user and password (HTTP Basic); podnet
        connect sends them in the WebSocket upgrade. The file has the password
        on its first line and mode 0600. (tunnel, serve, share, demo, connect)
    PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
        A token for the relay of --transport relay. It goes only in the
        X-Relay-Token header. Without it, podnet mints a token with POST
        /v1/mint on the relay and keeps it in relay-token-HOST.json (mode
        0600) in the state directory. (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    PODNET_RELAY_CONNECT_TOKEN
        The connect token of a pair, for the operator side of the reverse
        relay. It goes only in the X-Relay-Token header. Without it, podnet
        reads the local pair file. (relay connect)
    PODNET_NETNS_TEST_MEM
        A test hook of the seccomp backend: no-fd does not open the memory of
        the program for writing (process_vm_writev is used); none also does
        not use process_vm_writev (getsockname and getpeername fail with
        EOPNOTSUPP). (pod (tests only))
    PODNET_TEST_UMASK
        A test hook of the unix listeners: the test of bind_private runs again
        in a new process with this umask (octal). (pod (tests only))
    PODNET_PROBE_CHILD
        Set by podnet for its own child process of a namespace probe (net,
        user-net or veth): the process runs the probe before main and exits
        with the result code. Do not set it. (pod (internal))
    PODNET_NETNS_TEST_NO_NETNS
        A test hook of --backend auto: set and not empty, the netns backend
        cannot run, and auto takes the seccomp backend. (pod (tests only))
    PODNET_NETNS_TEST_VETH
        A test hook of the netns backend: set and not empty, the namespace
        uses the veth wire (a veth pair and a packet socket) also when it can
        open /dev/net/tun. (pod (tests only))
    PODNET_WARP_API
        The one base of the WARP API: https://HOST[:PORT] (http:// for a
        loopback host only). Without it, podnet tries
        https://api.cloudflareclient.com, then
        https://api.devices.cloudflare.com after a dial, TLS or 5xx failure.
        Another value is a configuration error (exit 78). (warp (each command
        that calls the WARP API))
    PODNET_WARP_TCP_BURST
        The TCP window of the userspace stack of WARP, in segments of the MTU:
        a number from 1 to 430, or none (no limit, the default): for a
        measurement of throughput. Another value is a configuration error
        (exit 78). (warp proxy, warp run, warp up, agent up)
    PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT
        The value of --masque-transport: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the default)
        or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443; each IP packet is an HTTP datagram). h3 has
        no relay and no proxy. (warp (each command that opens a MASQUE
        session), warp up (its proxy))
    PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT, PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT
        The value of --transport (masque, the default, or wireguard) and of
        --wireguard-endpoint (IP:PORT). wireguard carries the tunnel on UDP to
        the WireGuard front door (port 2408 of the record) with the device of
        warp export (warp-wg.json of the state directory), which podnet
        registers when the file has none. It has no relay and no proxy. (warp
        (each command that opens a session), warp up (its proxy))
    PODNET_WARP_CARRY, PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT
        The value of --carry (none, or wg) and of --carry-endpoint (IP:PORT).
        wg: a second WireGuard device (warp-carry.json of the state directory,
        registered when the file has none) goes inside the tunnel, on a UDP
        socket of the first stack; the tools use the stack of the second
        device (IPv4, MTU 1200). Its exit is the exit of the second device.
        With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. (warp (each
        command with a userspace stack), warp up (its proxy))
    PODNET_WARP_L4_FORM
        The form of the CONNECT of the L4 door, for a test of the door: plain
        (RFC 9114, the default), extended (:protocol cf-connect-tcp) or header
        (cf-connect-proto: cf-connect-tcp). (warp proxy --l4)
    PODNET_WARP_L4
        Set to true: the value of --l4. Each TCP client of the proxy is one
        HTTP/3 CONNECT stream to the L4 door of WARP on UDP 443 (TLS name of
        --l4-sni), with no IP stack; UDP is not served. (warp proxy)
    PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE
        The value of --session-max-age: each MASQUE session is closed on
        purpose at this age (seconds), and a new one opens, with a new egress
        address. The TCP flows of the old session end. Off when not set. (warp
        proxy, warp forward, warp run, warp up)
    PODNET_WARP_CC
        The value of --cc: the congestion controller of the TCP connections of
        the userspace stack of WARP, for the data that the stack sends: none
        (the default; only the window of the peer limits it), reno (RFC 5681)
        or cubic (RFC 9438). Another value is a configuration error (exit 78).
        (warp (each command with a userspace stack), warp up (its proxy),
        tunnel --transport warp)
    PODNET_WARP_NO_CHECK
        Set and not empty: a new MASQUE session is used with no check of its
        data path. By default, one DNS query through the session must get an
        answer (5 s) before the session is up; else the session is closed and
        podnet tries again. For a measurement. (warp proxy, warp run, warp up,
        warp probe, warp exit, warp nc, agent up)
    PODNET_NETNS_QUIET
        Set and not empty: the pod prints no warnings (errors stay). podnet -q
        sets it. (pod, warp exec, warp shell, warp run)
    PODNET_PROXY_USER, PODNET_PROXY_PASSWORD_FILE
        The value of --proxy-user and --proxy-password-file: each client of
        the proxy must give this user and the password on the first line of
        the file (mode 0600), with SOCKS5 (RFC 1929) or HTTP Basic. A client
        with no or wrong credentials gets 0xff, 0x01 or 407. (warp proxy, warp
        up)
    PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME, PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL,
    PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE
        The value of --device-name, --device-model and --device-locale: what a
        new device declares at its registration (a name of 1 to 64 characters,
        a model of 1 to 32, a locale as en_US). With none, the request is as
        before (model PC, locale en_US, no name). A bad value is a usage error
        (exit 64). A saved device does not change. (warp (each command that
        registers a device), tunnel --transport warp)
    PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT, PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE
        The value of --fragment-client-hello (off, record or sni) and
        --fragment-size (N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 bytes; default 64-160): the
        TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection goes in more than one record.
        sni ends the first record in the server name. A bad value is a
        configuration error (exit 78). (warp (each command that opens a MASQUE
        session), warp up (its proxy))
    PODNET_WARP_RULES, PODNET_WARP_RULES_FILE
        The value of -r/--rule (comma-separated KIND:VALUE=ACTION) and of
        --rules-file: the rules of the destinations of the proxy. KIND is
        domain or cidr (IPv4, IPv6, or @FILE of prefixes); ACTION is tunnel,
        direct or reject. The file is read again when it changes. A bad rule
        is a usage error (exit 64). (warp proxy, warp up (its proxy reads
        them))
    PODNET_WARP_FORWARD
        The value of -L/--local, comma-separated: LISTEN=HOST:PORT. Each
        connection to LISTEN (PORT on 127.0.0.1, ADDR:PORT, tcp://ADDR:PORT or
        unix:/PATH) goes through WARP to HOST:PORT; HOST is resolved inside
        the tunnel. A loopback target is a usage error (exit 64). (warp
        forward)
    PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS
        The value of --resolver: the DNS resolvers inside the tunnel,
        comma-separated, in place of 1.1.1.1:53. IP[:PORT] is DNS on UDP;
        tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] is DNS over TLS (RFC 7858, port 853), with the
        certificate checked for NAME or the IP address. The first that answers
        wins. warp tun --default-route writes the UDP ones on port 53 to
        resolv.conf. (warp proxy, warp up, warp run, warp tun, warp probe,
        warp nc, tunnel --transport warp)
    PODNET_UDP
        QUIC on UDP 7844: off (no QUIC on UDP 7844), on (no probe), or probe
        (the default). With probe and --protocol auto, podnet sends one QUIC
        packet to the edge while it starts; when the send or the path refuses
        it, podnet does not try QUIC on UDP 7844. No answer keeps the order of
        the legs. Another value is a configuration error (exit 78). podnet
        doctor shows the quic leg refused with off; podnet net doctor always
        sends its probe. (tunnel, serve, share, demo, doctor)
    PODNET_ERROR_PROGRAM
        A program that gets a JSON report on its stdin when podnet fails (exit
        code not 0). It runs with no shell and no arguments, for at most 30 s.
        The report has the version, the system, the command, the exit code,
        the error ("error": the error and its causes, once) and the log lines
        before it ("messages": at most 64), with credentials masked. A usage
        error (exit 64) sends a report too. The program does not get
        TUNNEL_TOKEN, the relay tokens, or a proxy variable with a user and a
        password. (all commands)
    PODNET_VERIFY_STRICT
        When set and not 0: a verify that only failed at name resolution, or
        at the CONNECT of a proxy, is an error (exit 69). By default the
        tunnel stays up, and the log says that the URL is not proved. (tunnel,
        serve, share, demo)
    RUST_LOG
        The log filter, for example podnet=debug. The default is podnet=info.
        (all commands)
    PODNET_DEBUG
        When set, log each visitor channel of the SSH relay transport. (serve
        (SSH relay))
    PAGER, TERM, LESS, LINES
        The pager of podnet man on a terminal: PAGER (empty or cat: no pager),
        else less when PATH has it and TERM is not dumb, else the built-in
        pager. When LESS is not set, less gets LESS=FRX. The built-in pager
        shows LINES lines (default: the terminal height). (man)
    PATH
        podnet pod finds the program to run in PATH. podnet man finds less,
        and podnet net shim finds the C compiler. (pod, man, net shim)
    CC
        The C compiler that builds the LD_PRELOAD shims. The default is cc,
        then gcc, then clang. (net shim, net socksify, net passwd-shim, net
        ts-shims)
    USER
        The default login name of the synthetic user. (net passwd-shim, net
        ts-shims)
    LD_PRELOAD
        The printed environment adds the shim in front of the current value.
        (net shim, net socksify)
    PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN
        The shared token of a TCP switch, when --switch-token-file is not
        given. net switch --listen tcp://... needs it (else exit 64), and each
        TCP peer sends it first; a peer with no token or a wrong one is
        closed. A unix switch needs no token: it takes the same user only.
        (net switch, net proxy --switch)
    PODNET_VNET_SHIM, PODNET_SOCKS_SHIM
        The path of a shim that is already built. podnet uses it instead of a
        build. (net shim, net socksify)
    PODNET_VNET_LOG, PODNET_VNET_MAP_LOOPBACK, PODNET_VNET_LOCAL_ADDR,
    PODNET_VNET_PREFIX, PODNET_VNET_HOSTS, PODNET_VNET_CONTROL,
    PODNET_VNET_MAX_FDS, PODNET_VNET_SOCKS, PODNET_VNET_SOCKS_ROUTES
        The shim of the virtual network: log each translation; map 127.0.0.1
        to the local virtual address; the local virtual IPv4 address; the
        prefix of the abstract names; a name=address table; the abstract name
        of the control socket; the size of the descriptor table; the unix
        socket of a SOCKS5 front door; the comma list of destinations
        (tailnet, ADDR, ADDR/BITS, IPV4:PORT, [IPV6]:PORT) whose stream
        connects go to that door (net shim --socks-route). (libpodnet-vnet.so)
    PODNET_SOCKS_PROXY, PODNET_SOCKS_LOG, PODNET_SOCKS_ALL,
    PODNET_SOCKS_CIDRS, PODNET_SOCKS_MAX_FDS
        The socks shim: the unix socket of the SOCKS5 front door; log each
        route and each redirect; redirect each connect; redirect only the
        destinations of a comma list (tailnet, ADDR, ADDR/BITS, IPV4:PORT,
        [IPV6]:PORT; net socksify --cidr) in place of the tailnet default; the
        size of the descriptor table. (libpodnet-socks.so)
    SANDHOME_PASSWD, UNIXSOCKD_LOG
        The passwd file that fakepwd.so reads; log each connection of
        unixsockd. (net passwd-shim, net ts-shims, unixsockd)
    PODNET_BUILD_COMMIT
        Read when podnet is compiled: the commit that --version prints. (the
        build)
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
        Read when podnet is compiled: the date of the manual (podnet man
        --roff). Without it, the date of the commit. (the build)

FILES
    <state directory>/warp.json
        The WARP device, its token and its MASQUE key (mode 0600, directory
        mode 0700). The state directory is the first that podnet can write of
        PODNET_STATE_DIR, $XDG_STATE_HOME/podnet, $HOME/.local/state/podnet,
        $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet and podnet-<uid> in the temporary directory;
        never the current directory. podnet warp writes it; podnet warp delete
        removes it. --identity names another file.
    $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/warp-up.json, else
    $TMPDIR/podnet-<uid>/warp-up.json
        The pointer file of podnet warp up (mode 0600, directory mode 0700):
        its socket and its state directory. warp exec, warp shell, warp nc and
        agent read it last, so that they find a podnet warp up with another
        state directory. podnet reads it only when this user owns it and no
        other user can read it. podnet warp down removes it.
    <state directory>/link-identity.key
        The Ed25519 key of this install for podnet link (mode 0600; a wider
        mode exits 71). podnet link listen, dial and status --create make it
        on first use. podnet link status prints its fingerprint. The seed is
        never printed, logged or put in JSON.
    <run directory>/link-PID.ctl, link-PID.ctl.token (podnet link listen
    --control, link connect --control)
        The control socket of a link instance (mode 0600) and its token (32
        random bytes in hex, mode 0600, new for each run). One JSON object for
        each line: status, peer, open. A request is 4 KiB at most, an answer
        64 KiB, 16 clients; the user of the peer must be the user of the
        instance or root; a wrong token exits 77. The instance removes both
        files at its stop. There is no TCP listener and no HTTP endpoint.
    ALLOW (podnet link listen --allow, podnet link dial --allow)
        An allow list of the link: one peer on each line (the fingerprint of
        podnet link status, a SHA256: fingerprint, or a key in hex), 4096
        lines at most. A line that starts with # is a comment. The list is
        default deny. The file must belong to this user and must not be
        writable by others (exit 71); a missing file exits 66.
    podnet-ca.pem (beside the binary)
        Extra TLS roots (PEM), for example the root of a TLS-inspecting proxy.
        podnet reads it when --ca-file and SSL_CERT_FILE are not set.
    /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
        The first system bundle of TLS roots. podnet also tries
        /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt,
        /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem,
        /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem, /etc/ssl/cert.pem and
        /usr/local/share/certs/ca-root-nss.crt, and reads the first that it
        can.
    config.yml (--config)
        A cloudflared configuration file: tunnel, credentials-file,
        ha-connections, protocol, ingress. The path: of an ingress rule is a
        regular expression, as in cloudflared; it matches a part of the
        request path (^/api/ for a prefix).
    ~/.cloudflared/<tunnel-id>.json (--credentials-file)
        The credentials of a named tunnel, as cloudflared writes them.
    /tmp/podnet-vnet.socks
        The default listen address of podnet net proxy.
    /tmp/podnet-vnet.switch
        The default listen address of podnet net switch.
    /tmp/podnet-socks.sock
        The default listen address of podnet net tailscale.
    /tmp/podnet-warp-<pid>.sock
        The proxy socket of podnet warp run, for the life of the command.
    $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet-netns-inbound/<port>.sock, else
    $TMPDIR/podnet-netns-inbound-<uid>/<port>.sock
        A port that a program under podnet pod listens on (--inbound-dir). The
        directory has mode 0700; a directory of another user, or one that the
        group or others can write, is refused.
    $TMPDIR/podnet-vnet, $TMPDIR/podnet-socks, $TMPDIR/podnet-ts-shims
        The default build directories of the shims.

EXIT STATUS
    0 (success)
        The command completed. A server command (tunnel, serve, share, proxy)
        exits 0 when it is stopped with Ctrl-C or when --run-for ends.
    1 (failure)
        A failure that has no other code. With --check: a check of an origin
        or of the network failed (a bad flag or configuration has its own
        code).
    3 (no-backend)
        podnet pod and podnet warp run: no backend can run on this host, the
        program is not in PATH (or cannot run), or the setup of the backend
        failed. pod doctor gives 3 when no backend can run.
    64 (usage)
        A bad command line: an unknown command or flag, a missing or bad
        value. Nothing was done.
    66 (no-input)
        A file that must exist is missing: the key of the link where a command
        needs an existing key, or the allow list of the link.
    68 (no-host)
        The address of a peer does not resolve.
    69 (unavailable)
        A service or a network path is not available: no edge leg worked, the
        quick-tunnel service, the WARP API or the MASQUE endpoint did not
        answer.
    71 (os-error)
        A file of the host cannot be used: a key file or an allow list with a
        mode that lets other users change it (the key: any access), a symbolic
        link in place of the file, or a file of another user. The file is not
        replaced.
    75 (tempfail)
        The quick-tunnel service refused a provision for now (HTTP 429): the
        error report (PODNET_ERROR_PROGRAM) has retry_after_s. Also: --detach
        lost the pipe to the command that started it. Try again later.
    77 (no-permission)
        A peer is not in the allow list of the link (default deny). Nothing of
        a service was offered to it.
    78 (config)
        A configuration that cannot be used: a variable of the environment
        such as PODNET_EDGE, a configuration file given with --config, a
        tunnel token or a credentials file (as a flag or as a key of the
        file), or a roots file of --ca-file.
    124 (timeout)
        --detach: the instance was not ready in --ready-timeout seconds (it is
        stopped), as timeout(1) exits.

EXAMPLES
    Test the path from this host to the edge; the last line names the step to
    take.
        $ podnet doctor

    In a sandbox: test what works, start WARP when it is needed, and print the
    commands to use.
        $ podnet agent up

    A quick tunnel in the background: one JSON document with the URL, then
    exit 0.
        $ podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --detach

    The instances that run in the background, as one JSON document.
        $ podnet ps --json

    Ask the relay for a pair: a name, and the tokens of the node and of the
    operator.
        $ podnet relay pair

    Give the SSH server of this host to the operators of the pair, through the
    relay.
        $ podnet relay node --to 127.0.0.1:22

    Publish a unix socket through the default SSH relay (pinggy). The
    endpoint, the user and the URL rule are data of pod-services. The URL is
    in the ready document; podnet ps shows the URL after each reconnect.
        $ podnet ssh-relay --socket /run/user/1000/origin.sock --detach

    Publish a unix socket through a named SSH relay. podnet tries its plain
    SSH endpoints in order.
        $ podnet ssh-relay --service serveo --socket
        /run/user/1000/origin.sock --detach

    Publish a unix socket through an SSH relay that pod-services does not
    know: give the server, the user and the URL rule.
        $ podnet ssh-relay --server relay.example.net:443 --user podnet
        --url-skip dashboard.example.net --socket /run/user/1000/origin.sock
        --detach

    Say whether a newer release exists. podnet update installs it after it
    checks the cosign signature and the SHA-256.
        $ podnet update --check

    Make a quick tunnel to the built-in origin, and fetch its public URL.
        $ podnet demo --exit-on-verify

    A quick tunnel to a local HTTP server.
        $ podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080

    A quick tunnel to an HTTP server on a unix socket.
        $ podnet tunnel --unix /run/app.sock

    Use the HTTP/2 edge leg on TCP 7844 (no UDP).
        $ podnet tunnel --protocol http2 --url http://127.0.0.1:8080

    Reach the edge through WARP on TCP 443 only.
        $ podnet tunnel --transport warp --hello-world

    A named tunnel.
        $ podnet tunnel --token TOKEN --url http://127.0.0.1:8080

    Ingress rules from a cloudflared configuration file.
        $ podnet tunnel --config config.yml

    Carry a raw stream through the quick tunnel.
        $ podnet tunnel --forward unix:/run/app.sock

    The client side of --forward.
        $ podnet connect wss://NAME.trycloudflare.com/__podnet/ws -L
        tcp://127.0.0.1:8080

    Serve a directory.
        $ podnet serve --dir ./public

    Serve a directory to this host only, on a local listener. No tunnel.
        $ podnet serve --dir ./public --local 127.0.0.1:8080

    Serve a directory on a unix socket. No tunnel.
        $ podnet serve --dir ./public --local unix:/run/site.sock

    Make the bare repository ./repos/app.git.
        $ podnet git init --root ./repos app

    Serve the repositories through a quick tunnel: anyone can clone, the user
    me can push.
        $ podnet git serve --root ./repos --anon-read --push-user me
        --push-password-file ./pass

    Serve the repositories over SSH through a relay pair: ssh -o
    ProxyCommand='podnet relay connect NAME'.
        $ podnet git serve --root ./repos --ingress relay --authorized-keys
        ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

    The clone URLs of each repository, and the fingerprint of the SSH host
    key.
        $ podnet git urls --root ./repos

    Receive files, with a PIN.
        $ podnet share --mode upload --password

    Share an HTTP server on a unix socket, behind a PIN.
        $ podnet share --mode proxy --unix /run/api.sock

    The WARP device and account.
        $ podnet warp status

    A SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT proxy through WARP.
        $ podnet warp proxy --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:40000

    Run a program with its traffic through WARP.
        $ podnet warp run -- curl https://www.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace

    Run a program with all its traffic through a proxy.
        $ podnet pod -x socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 -- curl https://example.com

    A virtual address for a real service.
        $ podnet net proxy --forward 10.66.0.2:8080=unix:/run/app.sock

    A switch on TCP. Each stack gives the same token: --switch-token-file, or
    PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN.
        $ podnet net switch --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:7000 --switch-token-file
        /run/secrets/switch

    A link listener on a unix socket (mode 0600). A peer must prove its key
    and be in peers.txt.
        $ podnet link listen /run/user/1000/app.sock --allow peers.txt --to
        unix:/run/user/1000/origin.sock --detach

    Connect to a link listener, check its key, and print its fingerprint.
        $ podnet link dial /run/user/1000/app.sock --peer FINGERPRINT --check

    Hold a link to a listener and run a control socket for it.
        $ podnet link connect /run/user/1000/app.sock --peer FINGERPRINT
        --control /run/user/1000/link.ctl --detach --name peer1

    Open one stream of the link to the peer for each connection to
    127.0.0.1:8080, for the service http of the peer. A running link connect
    or link listen instance holds the link (PODNET_LINK_CONTROL names its
    control socket).
        $ podnet forward -L 8080=peer:FINGERPRINT/http

    One JSON line about this host, for a program.
        $ podnet status

    This manual as a man(7) page.
        $ podnet man --roff


SEE ALSO
    podnet pod --help; cloudflared(1); https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet
    (README.md, the topic documents in docs/, docs/protocol.md,
    docs/virtual-network.md).
```

<!-- document: README.md -->

# podnet

`podnet` is the Swiss army knife of networking for restricted hosts. It is one static binary for Linux
that brings its own network to a host that has no `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, no TUN device, no UDP, no DNS
resolver, or only a proxy to go out. With it you can publish a local service, reach out to the internet,
run a program through a proxy, join a tailnet, route flows over many ways out, and check which of these
work on the host. It needs no root and no other program.

* Publish: Cloudflare quick tunnels and named tunnels (the work of `cloudflared`), a file server, file
  transfer with a PIN, git hosting, and inbound TCP through a relay.
* Reach out: the Cloudflare WARP client with no root (`podnet warp`), proxy chains, Tailscale and NetBird
  with no TUN, DNS over HTTPS, and TCP and UDP forwards.
* Contain: `podnet pod` runs any program (also a static binary) with all its traffic sent through a
  proxy. `podnet net` gives a program IP addresses on a host that refuses `AF_INET` binds.
* Route: `podnet route` is a router of networks, groups, policies, health probes and doors, with a
  kernel mode.
* Check: `podnet doctor` tests the path to the edge, `podnet pod doctor` and `podnet net doctor` test the
  host, and `podnet bench` measures a way out.

The license is 0BSD. podnet is for Linux only. The binary has no run-time dependency on the C library.

## Install

Each [release](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/releases) has static binaries for `x86_64`,
`aarch64`, `armv7`, `riscv64gc`, `i686`, `arm` (ARMv6), `loongarch64` and `powerpc64le`. The install
script downloads the newest one for this machine, checks its SHA-256 (and the cosign signature when
`cosign` is present), runs it, and then puts it in place:

```sh
s=$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PodUtils/podnet/main/scripts/install.sh) && sh -c "$s"
```

Do not use `curl URL | sh` in a script: a pipe has the exit status of `sh`, and `sh` exits 0 when `curl`
fails. There is also a container image, `ghcr.io/podutils/podnet:beta` (`FROM scratch`).

Verify a download by hand:

```sh
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/vX.Y.Z \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com SHA256SUMS
```

Update in place. `podnet update` checks the cosign certificate and signature over `SHA256SUMS`, the
SHA-256 of the binary, and that the new binary runs; `--rollback` puts the old binary back:

```sh
podnet update --check
podnet update
```

[docs/install.md](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/install.md) gives the install script
options, the release files, the provenance check, the notebook cell for hosts that lose their disk, the
image, `podnet update` and the rebuild of a release.

## Quick start

```sh
podnet doctor                                   # which ways out work from this host
podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080       # a public URL (quick tunnel, no account)
podnet serve ./public                           # serve a directory on a public URL
podnet share --file ./report.pdf --password     # send one file; the visitor needs a PIN
podnet warp up && eval "$(podnet warp env)"     # the internet through WARP, with no root
podnet pod -x socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 -- curl https://example.com   # any program through a proxy
podnet agent up --expose 3000                   # a sandbox: test, start WARP if needed, expose a port
podnet man                                      # the manual
```

## What podnet does

| Area | Commands | Function | Document |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tunnels | `tunnel`, `demo`, `qr` | Quick tunnels and named tunnels to a local origin (HTTP, unix socket, TCP). | [tunnels](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/tunnels.md) |
| Raw streams | `tunnel --forward`, `connect` | SSH, databases and unix sockets through a quick tunnel. | [tunnels](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/tunnels.md) |
| File server, transfer, git | `serve`, `share`, `git` | Serve a directory, receive or send files with a PIN, host git repositories. | [serve](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/serve.md) |
| Publish by one word | `expose` | Publish a local service by a tunnel, the relay or a virtual address. | [forward](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/forward.md) |
| WARP | `warp register`, `proxy`, `forward`, `run`, `up`, `env`, `exec`, `shell`, `nc`, `tun`, `export`, `scan` | The Cloudflare WARP client on TCP 443, with no root and no TUN. | [warp](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/warp.md) |
| Pods | `pod`, `pod doctor` | Run a program with all its traffic sent through a proxy chain, with rules and audit. | [pods](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/pods.md) |
| Virtual networks | `net proxy`, `switch`, `shim`, `doctor` | IP addresses for programs on a host that refuses `AF_INET` binds. | [networks](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/networks.md) |
| Overlays | `net tailscale`, `net socksify`, `netbird:`, `wg:` | Tailscale, NetBird and WireGuard on a host with no TUN. | [networks](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/networks.md) |
| Router | `route --config`, `--check --to`, `--status`, `--export` | Networks, groups, policies, health, doors, DNS door, kernel mode. | [router](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/router.md) |
| Forwards | `forward -L`, `forward --dns` | TCP and UDP forwards and a DNS door through a network. | [forward](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/forward.md) |
| Relays | `relay pair`, `node`, `connect`, `ssh-relay` | Inbound TCP to a host with outbound HTTPS only; an SSH forward relay. | [relay](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/relay.md) |
| Link | `link listen`, `connect`, `dial`, `status`, `close`, `carriers`, `peer:FP/SERVICE` | A link between two installs over a carrier (unix socket, memory): each end proves its Ed25519 key, and an allow list (default deny) admits the peers. A control socket shows the links. `forward -L PORT=peer:FP/SERVICE` reaches a service of a peer. | [link](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/link.md) |
| Networks and `--egress` | `--egress`, `--proxy`, `--resolve` | One spec for each way out: direct, proxy URL, relay, `tailscale:`, `netbird:`, `wg:`, `unix:`. | [egress](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/egress.md), [proxies](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/proxies.md) |
| Background | `--detach`, `ps`, `logs`, `wait`, `stop`, `autostart` | Run a command in the background, restart it, start it at boot. | [background](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/background.md) |
| Checks | `doctor`, `doctor --agent`, `status`, `ports`, `bench`, `bug-report`, `agent up` | Test the host, the path to the edge and a way out. | [doctor](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/doctor.md) |
| Update | `update` | Replace the binary after a check of the signature. | [install](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/install.md) |
| Manual | `man`, `--help --json`, `completions` | The manual, JSON help, the llms files, exit codes. | [cli](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/cli.md) |

## Limits that podnet handles

| Limit on the host | Part of podnet |
| --- | --- |
| No UDP to the edge | The HTTP/2 edge leg on TCP 7844. |
| Only TCP 443 out | The QUIC edge leg inside WARP (MASQUE), or the WebSocket relay. |
| No DNS resolver | DNS over HTTPS by IP address, then a static edge list. |
| Egress through a proxy only | HTTP `CONNECT`, SOCKS5, Digest, unix-socket and command proxies, and `NO_PROXY`. |
| No root, no TUN, no network namespace | `podnet pod` (seccomp backend), `podnet warp run`. |
| No `AF_INET` bind | `podnet net` (shim and userspace stack), unix-socket origins. |

One limit stays: a proxy that terminates TLS cannot carry the edge connection or the MASQUE connection,
because both need the Cloudflare certificate chain. A quick tunnel is for tests and development: it has
no uptime guarantee, at most 200 requests in flight (more get `429`), and no Server-Sent Events
([limits](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/protocol.md#7-limits-of-quick-tunnels)).
[docs/target-environment.md](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/blob/main/docs/target-environment.md) gives
the measured hosts. The workflow `.github/workflows/live.yml` runs `podnet demo` with each edge leg on a
GitHub runner on each push and each day.

# Install, update and verify

This page gives the ways to get `podnet`, to check a download, to update the binary and to
rebuild a release.

## Release binaries

Each [release](https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/releases) has static
Linux binaries of `podnet` for `x86_64`, `aarch64`, `armv7`,
`riscv64gc`, `i686`, `arm` (ARMv6, hard float), `loongarch64` and
`powerpc64le`. podnet is for Linux only. This page describes `main`; the notes in `docs/releases/` say what
a tag has. Each release also has these files:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `SHA256SUMS` | The SHA-256 of each binary and of `podnet.1`. |
| `SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json` | The keyless cosign signature of `SHA256SUMS`. |
| `provenance.sigstore.json` | The SLSA provenance of the binaries. |
| `podnet.1` | The manual page (`podnet man --roff`). |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` | The index, and the manual with the documents, for agents. |
| `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` | The license texts of the crates in the binaries. |

Verify the files before you use them. Download the binary, `SHA256SUMS` and
the two bundles to one directory. Then do these steps:

1. Check the checksums. The command ignores the files that you did not
   download:

   ```sh
   sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
   ```

2. Check the signature of `SHA256SUMS`. Replace `vX.Y.Z` with the tag:

   ```sh
   cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
     --certificate-identity https://github.com/PodUtils/podnet/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/vX.Y.Z \
     --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com SHA256SUMS
   ```

3. Check the provenance of the binary (gh 2.49 or later):

   ```sh
   gh attestation verify podnet-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo PodUtils/podnet \
     --signer-workflow PodUtils/podnet/.github/workflows/release.yml
   ```

   With no network access to the GitHub API, give the bundle and a trusted
   root. Make `trusted_root.jsonl` on a host with network access
   (`gh attestation trusted-root > trusted_root.jsonl`), and copy it:

   ```sh
   gh attestation verify podnet-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo PodUtils/podnet \
     --signer-workflow PodUtils/podnet/.github/workflows/release.yml \
     --bundle provenance.sigstore.json --custom-trusted-root trusted_root.jsonl
   ```

A binary that has one changed byte fails each check. The workflow
`.github/workflows/release-proofs.yml` does these checks on a fresh runner
after each release. It also does each check on a changed copy, which must
fail.

## Install script

`scripts/install.sh` installs the binary of the newest release
(prereleases too) for this machine. It is POSIX `sh`:

```sh
s=$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PodUtils/podnet/main/scripts/install.sh) && sh -c "$s"
```

With wget: `s=$(wget -qO- URL) && sh -c "$s"`. Do not use `curl URL | sh`
in a script or a CI step: a pipe has the exit status of `sh`, and `sh`
exits 0 when `curl` fails or is missing.

* It uses the first downloader that it finds: `curl`, `wget`, `aria2c`,
  `http` (HTTPie), `python3`, `python` or `perl` (`HTTP::Tiny` with TLS),
  and last `busybox wget` (also a `wget` that is the busybox applet: it
  goes after `python3`, `python` and `perl`).
  HTTPS only; redirects to plain HTTP are refused. busybox wget does not
  check TLS certificates: the script says so in a warning, and with no
  `cosign` the check of `SHA256SUMS` then does not protect the download. A
  busybox with no TLS (no `ssl_client`) is not used.
* It checks the binary against `SHA256SUMS` (`sha256sum`, `shasum`,
  `openssl`, `busybox` or `python3`), and the cosign signature of
  `SHA256SUMS` when `cosign` is installed. A failed check stops it, and
  cosign then shows its output.
* It runs the new binary (`--version`) in the install directory before it
  replaces the old binary. A binary that does not run on this machine, or
  that does not print `podnet VERSION` of the release, does not replace the
  old one. The copy is a new file from `mktemp` with mode 0755 (also with
  a restrictive umask). When the path of the binary is a directory or
  another file that is not a regular file, the script stops before the
  downloads.
* The directory: `PODNET_INSTALL_DIR`, else `/usr/local/bin` for root, else
  `$XDG_BIN_HOME`, else `~/.local/bin`. A line says how to add it to `PATH`.
  The script checks the directory before the downloads.
* `PODNET_VERSION=<TAG>` (for example `v0.4.0-beta.1`) installs that release, with no request to
  the GitHub API. For the newest release, the script reads the API; when
  the API refuses (403 on a shared address), it reads `releases.atom`.
  A draft release is not used.
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` goes to `api.github.com` only. The token is
  not in the trace of `DEBUG=1` and not in the arguments of the downloader:
  curl reads it from stdin, wget from a private file.
* `PODNET_DOWNLOADER=wget` selects the downloader.
* A missing file of the release, an empty download and a failed download
  have different messages. INT, TERM and HUP stop the script and remove its files.

## Ephemeral hosts

A hosted notebook, a rebuilt container or a CI job can lose its disk at
each start. Then three things go:

* The binary: give `PODNET_INSTALL_DIR` a directory that stays.
* The WARP device: give `PODNET_STATE_DIR` (or `--identity PATH`) a directory
  that stays. Without it, each start registers a new anonymous device (the
  service limits new devices; see [warp.md](warp.md)). `PODNET_STATE_DIR=none` uses a new
  device on purpose.
* The release list: a pinned `PODNET_VERSION` uses no GitHub API.

This cell (Python 3, no curl) installs podnet in `KEEP`. The same cell is in
`notebooks/install.ipynb`. It fails when the install fails (`check=True`):

```python
# Install podnet on a host that loses its disk at each start (a notebook).
# KEEP is a directory that stays, for example a mounted drive.
import os
import subprocess
import urllib.request

KEEP = os.environ.get("PODNET_KEEP", os.path.expanduser("~/podnet-keep"))
VERSION = "latest"  # A tag (for example v0.4.0-beta.1) uses no GitHub API.
URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PodUtils/podnet/main/scripts/install.sh"

os.makedirs(os.path.join(KEEP, "bin"), exist_ok=True)
script = os.path.join(KEEP, "install.sh")
with open(script, "wb") as f:
    f.write(urllib.request.urlopen(URL, timeout=60).read())
env = dict(os.environ, PODNET_INSTALL_DIR=os.path.join(KEEP, "bin"), PODNET_VERSION=VERSION)
subprocess.run(["sh", script], env=env, check=True)

# The binary and the WARP device stay in KEEP.
os.environ["PATH"] = os.path.join(KEEP, "bin") + ":" + os.environ["PATH"]
os.environ["PODNET_STATE_DIR"] = os.path.join(KEEP, "state")
print(subprocess.run(["podnet", "--version"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
```

## Container image

Each release has an image for each Linux architecture of the binaries:
`ghcr.io/podutils/podnet:<tag>` (a manifest list), `:<tag>-<arch>` for one
architecture (`amd64`, `arm64`, `armv7`, `armv6`, `386`, `riscv64`,
`ppc64le`, `loong64`), and `:beta` for the newest prerelease. `:latest` is
for the newest release that is not a prerelease. No such release exists
now, so `:latest` has no image. The image is `FROM scratch` with `podnet`
in `/usr/local/bin`. It runs as user 65534. The state
directory is the volume `/var/lib/podnet` (`PODNET_STATE_DIR`). The entry point
is `podnet`. In the container, podnet is PID 1 (no init): SIGTERM and SIGINT
stop it at each stage, also before the ready line (exit 143 and 130).

```sh
docker run --rm ghcr.io/podutils/podnet:beta --version
docker run -d --name warp -v podnet-state:/var/lib/podnet -p 127.0.0.1:40000:40000 \
    ghcr.io/podutils/podnet:beta warp proxy --listen tcp://0.0.0.0:40000
docker run --rm ghcr.io/podutils/podnet:beta demo --exit-on-verify
```

The proxy listens on all addresses of the container: publish the port on
127.0.0.1 only, or give `--proxy-user` and `--proxy-password-file`.

## Update

```sh
podnet update --check              # say whether a newer release exists
podnet update                      # install it
podnet update --version <TAG>      # install the release <TAG>
podnet update --rollback           # put the binary before the update back
```

`podnet update` installs a release only after these checks: the certificate
of `SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json` chains to the Fulcio roots of Sigstore and
names `release.yml` of this repository at the tag, the signature over
`SHA256SUMS` is valid, the SHA-256 of the binary is its line in
`SHA256SUMS`, and the new binary runs `--version` in 10 seconds, with no
stdin, exits 0 and prints the version of the tag. After the run, the file
must still be the same file (device and inode), a regular file of this
user that other users cannot write; else podnet stops. Then the binary before
is kept as `podnet.prev` beside it, and a rename puts the new binary (mode
0755, also with a restrictive umask) in place. `podnet update --rollback` puts `podnet.prev` back (it must pass the
same run first) and keeps the binary that was in place as `podnet.prev`;
it uses no network. podnet does not check the inclusion proof of the Rekor
log. A prerelease is
installed only with `--version`, or when the current binary is a
prerelease.

* `--version TAG` uses no request to the GitHub API: the URLs of the files
  follow from the tag. A tag with no release exits 69 ("no release has the
  tag"). A text that is not a tag (a `/`, a `..`, a character other than
  `0-9 A-Z a-z . + -`) exits 64. podnet skips such a tag in the API and in
  `releases.atom` too.
* With no `--version`, podnet reads the GitHub API, else `releases.atom` (the
  API answers 403 on a shared address; the feed has no quota).
* `--version` of the installed version says so and exits 0; `--force`
  installs it again. `--force` with no `--version` installs the newest
  release also when it is the installed version; it does not go back to
  an older release.
* The repository is fixed (it names the signer of the binary). podnet does
  not read `PODNET_REPO` (a variable of `scripts/install.sh`); a warning says
  so.

## Rebuild a release

`scripts/rebuild.sh TAG [TARGET]` rebuilds `podnet` of a
release from its tag, at another path, in the pinned image of
`images/build/Dockerfile` of the tag, with the command of `release.yml`.
The binary must have the SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS`. TARGET is
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` or `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (the default is
the one of the machine). It needs git, curl and docker
(`CONTAINER=podman` for podman). `release-proofs.yml` runs it for both
targets after each release.

```sh
sh scripts/rebuild.sh <TAG>
```

<!-- document: docs/tunnels.md -->

# Tunnels

This page gives the Cloudflare tunnels of `podnet`: origins, the configuration file, named
tunnels, the edge protocol, the credential in front of a tunnel and raw streams.


A quick tunnel (`podnet tunnel` with no account, a name under `*.trycloudflare.com`) is for tests and
development: no uptime guarantee, at most 200 requests in flight (more get `429`), no Server-Sent Events,
and the Cloudflare Online Services Terms ([limits and terms](protocol.md#7-limits-of-quick-tunnels)).
A named tunnel uses a Cloudflare account.

## Origins

```sh
podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080   # HTTP or HTTPS origin
podnet tunnel --port 8080                   # the same as http://127.0.0.1:8080
podnet tunnel --unix /run/app.sock          # HTTP origin on a unix socket
podnet tunnel --hello-world                 # built-in test origin
podnet tunnel --config ./config.yml         # cloudflared ingress rules
podnet tunnel --token "$T" --tcp 10.0.0.5:5432  # raw TCP origin (named tunnel)
```

A raw TCP origin (`--tcp host:port` or `tcp://host:port`) carries TCP and
WebSocket streams of a named tunnel (WARP routing, `cloudflared access
tcp`). A quick tunnel receives HTTP: podnet answers each HTTP request to a
raw TCP origin with 501, and does not verify the public URL. For TCP
through a quick tunnel, use `--forward` and `podnet connect` (see "Raw streams
through a quick tunnel" below).

The service strings are the same as in cloudflared:

```text
http://host:port     https://host:port     unix:/path/to.sock
unix+tls:/path.sock  tcp://host:port       http_status:404
hello_world          metrics               static:/srv/www
spa:/srv/www
```

* `static:` serves a directory.
* `spa:` serves a directory and sends `index.html` for unknown paths.
* `metrics` serves the Prometheus metrics of the tunnel.
  `podnet_decisions_total{decision,outcome}` counts the path decisions of
  the process: `dns` (`ip`, `pin`, `system`, `doh`, `fail`), `egress`
  (`direct`, `none`, `no_proxy`, `via`, `http`, `socks5`, `unix`, `exec`),
  `leg` (the leg that won), `masque` (`direct`, `relay`, `relay_first`,
  `no_relay`), `dispatch` (the requests of `warp proxy`) and `rule`. The
  health line of `warp proxy` has the same counters.
* `--http-host-header NAME` sets the `Host` header for the origin.
* `--no-tls-verify` does not verify the TLS certificate of an HTTPS origin.
* `--no-verify` (`tunnel`, `serve`, `share`, `demo`) does not fetch the public URL after the registration. The
  fetch proves that the URL answers. The flag does not change the check of an origin certificate: `--no-tls-verify`
  does that. Use `--no-verify` on a host that resolves a new `*.trycloudflare.com` name late.

All built-in origins run in the process. They do not open a TCP listener.

## Configuration file

`podnet tunnel --config` reads a cloudflared YAML file:

```yaml
tunnel: my-tunnel                      # the name or the UUID of the tunnel
credentials-file: /etc/podnet/creds.json
ha-connections: 2
protocol: auto
ingress:
  - hostname: app.example.com
    path: /api
    service: http://127.0.0.1:8080
    originRequest:
      noTLSVerify: true
      connectTimeout: 5s
  - service: http_status:404
```

* The origin is in the `ingress:` rules. With `--config`, the origin flags (`--url`, `--unix`, `--port`, `--tcp`,
  `--forward`, `--hello-world`, `--no-tls-verify`, `--http-host-header`, `--strip-accept-encoding`) are a usage
  error (exit 64): they would have no effect.
* The last rule must match all requests (no `hostname`, no `path`). podnet
  refuses a file where it does not.
* `path:` is a regular expression, as in cloudflared (the syntax of the
  Rust `regex` crate, which is close to Go RE2). It matches when it
  matches a part of the request path: `path: /api` also matches `/x/api`
  and `/apix`. Write `path: ^/api/` for the paths that start with `/api/`,
  and `path: ^/api$` for one path. A `.` matches each character: write
  `\.` for a dot. The query (from `?`) is not part of the path. The match
  reads the decoded path, as cloudflared does: `/a%20b` matches `^/a b$`
  (a `+` stays a `+`). A `path:` that is not a valid regular expression
  is an error at load (exit 78), with the file and the rule number.
* With no `ingress:`, `url:` gives one rule for each request (the same
  services as `service:`), and `hello-world: true` gives the hello-world
  page. `url:` or `hello-world:` with `ingress:` is an error.
* A file with no rule (no `ingress:`, `url:` or `hello-world:`) fails
  `--check` (exit 78) and the run.
* With `credentials-file:`, `tunnel:` is the name or the UUID of the tunnel,
  as in cloudflared. A UUID must be the `TunnelID` of the file. With
  `tunnel:` only, it is a tunnel token.
* `token:` is the tunnel token of a named tunnel. `token:` with
  `credentials-file:` is an error. With `token:`, a `tunnel:` must be the
  tunnel id of the token.
* With no `tunnel:`, no `credentials-file:` and no `token:`, podnet starts a
  quick tunnel. `--token`, `TUNNEL_TOKEN` and `--credentials-file` win over
  the file.
* podnet ignores the cloudflared keys that it does not use (`metrics`,
  `loglevel`, `warp-routing`, `tcpKeepAlive`, ...). Another key is an error
  (exit 78), with the nearest key. podnet checks the keys at the top level, in
  each ingress rule and in each `originRequest`.
* The top-level `originRequest` is the default of each rule. A key of the
  rule wins.
* `protocol:` and `ha-connections:` of the file are used. A flag
  (`--protocol`, `--ha-connections`) wins over the file.
* `--token` and `--credentials-file` on one command line are a usage error
  (exit 64). With the token from `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, `--credentials-file` wins,
  and a warning says so. A bad token or credentials file exits 78.
* A UTF-8 BOM at the start of the file is skipped. A list, an empty file, a
  rule with no `service`, a time with no unit (`connectTimeout: 5`) and a
  value of the wrong type each have their own message.

podnet reads the YAML with its own reader (`crates/podnet-core/src/yaml.rs`). The reader accepts
block mappings, block sequences, plain and quoted scalars on one line, and
comments. It refuses anchors, aliases, tags, block scalars (`|`, `>`), flow
collections that are not empty, tabs in the indentation, duplicate keys and
a document that nests deeper than 64 levels, and gives the line number.

## Named tunnels

A named tunnel uses a Cloudflare account and a hostname from the dashboard.

```sh
TUNNEL_TOKEN=<token> podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
podnet tunnel --token-file /run/secrets/tunnel-token --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
podnet tunnel --credentials-file ~/.cloudflared/<id>.json --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

`--token <token>` also works. Other users of the host can read a command
line, so `TUNNEL_TOKEN` or a file is safer. `--token-file PATH` (or
`TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE`) reads the token from a file; white space at the ends
is removed. `podnet relay connect --token-file PATH` reads a connect token,
and `podnet warp license -` reads the license key from stdin.

A command line of cloudflared works for a tunnel: `podnet tunnel run --token
T` is `podnet tunnel --token T`, `--no-autoupdate` is ignored, and
`--loglevel debug|info|warn|error` becomes `-v`, nothing or `-q`. Another
flag of cloudflared (`--logfile`, `--pidfile`, `--metrics`, ...) is a usage
error with the step to take in podnet.

## Edge protocol and transport

`--protocol` selects the protocol to the edge. `--transport` selects the
path.

| Leg | Socket on the host | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quic` | UDP 7844 | UDP to the edge is open. This is the fastest leg. |
| `http2` | TCP 7844, directly or through the proxy | UDP is blocked and TCP 7844 is open. |
| `quic+warp` | TCP 443 only (MASQUE) | Only TCP 443 is open. |
| `http2+relay` | TCP 443 to a WebSocket relay | Only TCP 443 is open, and WARP does not work (the proxy terminates TLS or takes names only). Only with `--transport relay`. |

With the default values (`--protocol auto --transport auto`), `podnet` tries the
legs in the order of the table, in a staggered race: the next leg starts when
the leg before has not registered in 2 seconds, or at once when it fails, and
the first leg that registers stays (`docs/protocol.md` section 3.3).
`--leg-failover serial` waits for each failure. The time limit of an attempt
is the budget of its leg: 130 seconds for `quic`, 280 seconds for `http2`
and `http2+relay` (`docs/protocol.md` section 3.3). Other values:

| `--protocol` | `--transport` | Legs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | `auto` | `quic`, `http2`, `quic+warp` |
| `quic` | `auto` | `quic`, `quic+warp` |
| `http2` | `auto` or `direct` | `http2` |
| `auto` | `direct` | `quic`, `http2` |
| `quic` | `direct` | `quic` |
| `auto` or `quic` | `warp` | `quic+warp` |
| `auto` or `http2` | `relay` | `http2+relay` |

`h2` is a name of `http2`. With a proxy, `auto` drops `quic` (see [proxies.md](proxies.md)); an explicit `--protocol quic` keeps it, and a warning says that
QUIC goes around the proxy.

`--transport relay` sends the HTTP/2 leg in a WebSocket to a
WebSocket-to-TCP relay on TCP 443 (`--relay URL`, or `PODNET_RELAY`; the
default is `https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev`). The relay opens TCP to the
edge on port 7844. The TLS to the edge is in the WebSocket, so the relay
does not see the tunnel. `PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN` gives a relay token; without
it, `podnet` mints one and keeps it in the state directory. When the relay
host does not answer, `podnet` tries other hosts of the same deployment (a
comma list in `--relay`, else the pool of the relay). The relay carries IPv4 TCP only, and it ends a
session after 64 MiB or 12 hours. Before that (at 60 MiB or 11.5 hours),
the tunnel connects a replacement edge connection, and the old one
finishes its open streams (`docs/protocol.md` section 3.4). A WARP
(MASQUE) session through the relay is replaced at the same limits: a new
session takes the new connections, and the open connections go on in the
old session for 90 s.

`--warp-identity PATH` keeps the WARP device in a file. Without it, each run
registers a new anonymous device. `PODNET_EDGE=ip:port,...` replaces edge
discovery.


## A credential in front of a tunnel

```sh
umask 077; printf '%s\n' 'a long password' > ~/.podnet-pass
podnet tunnel --port 3000 --auth-user me --auth-password-file ~/.podnet-pass
curl -u me:'a long password' https://<random>.trycloudflare.com/
```

* `--auth-user USER` and `--auth-password-file FILE` (`PODNET_AUTH_USER`,
  `PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE`) work with `tunnel`, `serve`, `share` and
  `demo`. Each request must give the user and the password (HTTP Basic).
  Else podnet answers 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="podnet"`, and
  the request reaches no origin. The origin does not get the
  `Authorization` header.
* The file has the password on its first line and mode 0600; else exit 78.
  The password is not on the command line.
* The check covers the HTTP origins and the `--forward` endpoint:
  `podnet connect --auth-user USER --auth-password-file FILE` sends the
  credential in the WebSocket upgrade. A raw `--tcp` origin carries no HTTP
  header: `--auth-user` with `--tcp` is a usage error (exit 64).
* The verify of the public URL takes the 401 as the normal answer.
* Basic goes in the TLS to the edge of Cloudflare: Cloudflare can see it.
  The credential does not hide the URL.

## Raw streams through a quick tunnel

A quick tunnel carries HTTP and WebSocket. `--forward` puts a WebSocket
endpoint at `/__podnet/ws`. `podnet connect` changes local sockets into
connections through that endpoint. Thus SSH, databases and unix sockets can
go through a quick tunnel.

```sh
# Server: expose a unix socket (or tcp://host:port).
podnet tunnel --forward unix:/run/app.sock

# Client: local port 8080 goes to that unix socket.
podnet connect wss://<random>.trycloudflare.com/__podnet/ws -L tcp://127.0.0.1:8080
```

The tunnel prints the endpoint (`podnet: forward  wss://...`). The ready
event of `--json`, the ready document of `--detach` and `podnet ps --json`
have it as `forward` (and `forward_path`); `podnet ps` shows it on a second
line.

`-L` accepts `tcp://[bind:]port` and `unix:///path` and is repeatable. Each
local connection gets its own WebSocket. `--forward` and an origin can be used
together: the origin gets all paths other than `/__podnet/ws`.

`podnet connect` dials as the other commands do: `--proxy` (or HTTPS_PROXY and
NO_PROXY), `--resolve`, the system resolver and DoH, and the roots of
`--ca-file`. At start, it opens one WebSocket to the remote and exits 69 when
the remote does not answer; `--no-check` starts without this check. A unix
socket that another process serves is refused (exit 69); `--replace` takes
it. At the end, podnet removes the socket files that it made. `--detach` and
`--name` work as for `tunnel` (see [background.md](background.md)); the ready
document has `remote`, `listen` and `listeners`. At `-v`, each WebSocket
logs the time of its TCP, TLS and upgrade steps.

`podnet connect URL --stdio` carries one stream on stdin and stdout, with no
listener. Use it as an SSH `ProxyCommand`:

```sh
ssh -o ProxyCommand='podnet connect wss://<random>.trycloudflare.com/__podnet/ws --stdio' user@host
```

The end of stdin closes the WebSocket. The close of the remote ends the
command. `--stdio` takes `--auth-user` and `--auth-password-file`. It exits
69 when the remote does not answer. It cannot be used with `-L` or
`--detach`.

## Other flags of `podnet tunnel`

* `--ha-connections N` (1 to 8; default 2, else `ha-connections` of `--config`): the number of edge
  connections. When the edge loses one, the others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of
  each request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections do not make one transfer faster.
* `--qr` prints the public URL as a QR code. `--json` prints JSON lines in place of text lines (see
  [cli.md](cli.md)). `--run-for SECONDS` stops the tunnel after that time.
* `--service-url URL` changes the provisioning endpoint of the quick tunnel (default
  `https://api.trycloudflare.com`), and `--user-agent TEXT` sets the `User-Agent` that podnet sends when it
  provisions (`docs/protocol.md` section 1).
* `--check` checks the plan and stops (see [cli.md](cli.md)).

## Other commands

```sh
podnet ports            # list the listening TCP ports (Linux)
podnet ports --probe    # only the ports that accept a connection
podnet qr <URL>         # print a QR code
```

`podnet expose TARGET` publishes a local service by one word ([forward.md](forward.md)).
`podnet ssh-relay` publishes a unix socket through an SSH relay ([relay.md](relay.md)).

<!-- document: docs/serve.md -->

# File server, file transfer and git hosting

This page gives `podnet serve` (a directory), `podnet share` (one transfer with a PIN)
and `podnet git` (git repositories). Each one has a local listener, a public quick tunnel
and the relay as roads to the visitors.

## Serve a directory

```sh
podnet serve ./public                   # DIR, or --dir DIR
podnet serve ./app --spa                # send index.html for unknown paths
podnet serve ./public --local 127.0.0.1:8080      # this host only, no tunnel
podnet serve ./public --local unix:/run/site.sock # a unix socket, no tunnel
podnet serve ./public --local 127.0.0.1:8080 --ingress tunnel  # both
podnet serve ./public --ingress relay --pair NAME     # through a relay pair
```

`--ingress` gives the road to the visitors:

* `tunnel` (the default with no `--local`): a public quick tunnel, or the
  named tunnel of `--token`.
* `relay`: the node of a relay pair (`podnet relay pair`). `--pair NAME`
  names the pair; the default is the pair with the most time left. The
  files listen on a private unix socket in the run directory, and the node
  connects each session of an operator to it. The operator runs
  `podnet relay connect NAME --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:8080` and opens
  `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`.
* `none` (the default with `--local`): only the local listeners.

`--local ADDR` (more than one is permitted) serves the same files on a
local listener:

* `ADDR` is `HOST:PORT`, `tcp://HOST:PORT` or `unix:PATH`.
* Port 0 takes a free port. podnet prints the bound address
  (`podnet: serve DIR on http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`). With `--json`, the
  `ready` line has `url` and `listen`.
* A unix socket has mode 0600. A socket that answers is refused (exit
  69; `--replace` takes it over). A stale socket is removed. A file that
  is not a socket is refused (exit 64). podnet removes its socket at the
  end.
* An address in use is refused (exit 69).
* `--check` is refused with `--local`, and is for `--ingress tunnel` only.
  With `--ingress none`, the tunnel flags have no effect, except `--auth-user`
  (see below). The `--json` ready line has `listens`, each listener.

`podnet serve` serves only the files in `--dir`:

* A symlink is served only when its real path is in `--dir`.
* A name that starts with a dot (`.git`, `.env`) is not served.
* Only regular files and directories are served (no FIFO, socket or
  device).

Each other path answers 404. With `--spa`, an unknown path answers the
`index.html` with status 200.

With `--tar`, `GET /PATH/?tar` gives the directory `PATH` as one ustar
archive (`application/x-tar`, `PATH.tar`). The archive has the same rules:
no dot name, no link out of `--dir`, no FIFO, socket or device. A link to a
directory is not followed. A name that does not fit in ustar (more than 255
bytes) is left out with a warning. Without `--tar`, `?tar` has no effect.

```sh
podnet serve --dir ./public --tar --local 127.0.0.1:8080
curl -fsS 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/docs/?tar' | tar -xf -
```

With `--list`, a directory with no `index.html` answers a listing of its
files. A browser gets HTML. A request with `Accept: application/json` gets
`{"path": "/docs/", "entries": [{"name", "type", "size", "modified"}]}`,
with `type` `dir` or `file` and `modified` in seconds after the Unix epoch.
The listing has the same rules: no dot name, no link out of `--dir`, no
FIFO, socket or device. A directory path with no `/` at its end goes to
the path with the `/` (308).

```sh
podnet serve --dir ./public --list --local 127.0.0.1:8080
curl -fsS -H 'Accept: application/json' http://127.0.0.1:8080/docs/
```

### Users, roles and a PIN

The file server checks its visitors itself, on each listener (`--local`,
the tunnel and the relay):

* `--users FILE`: the users (HTTP Basic). Each line is
  `USER:ROLE:HASH` or `USER:ROLE:@PASSWORD-FILE`. `ROLE` is `read` or
  `write`; a write user can also read. A relative `PASSWORD-FILE` starts at
  the directory of `FILE`. `FILE` and each password file must have mode
  0600. An empty line and a line that starts with `#` are skipped.
* `--auth-user USER --auth-password-file FILE`: one more user, with the
  write role.
* `--pin`: the files are locked with a 6-digit PIN, as `share --password`.
  podnet prints the PIN (`pin` in the `--json` line). With no users, the
  PIN gives the write role.
* `--anon-read`: a GET or HEAD needs no user and no PIN. A change still
  needs a write user (or the PIN).

A request with no user or a wrong password gets 401 with a Basic
challenge. A read user that sends a change gets 403.

`podnet serve --hash-password` reads a password from the first line of
stdin and prints its hash (`pbkdf2-sha256$ITERATIONS$SALT$KEY`, PBKDF2 with
HMAC-SHA256, hex):

```sh
printf '%s\n' "$PASSWORD" | podnet serve --hash-password
# pbkdf2-sha256$210000$...$...
install -m 600 /dev/null users
echo "alice:read:$(printf '%s\n' "$PASSWORD" | podnet serve --hash-password)" >> users
podnet serve --dir ./public --list --users users --local 127.0.0.1:8080
curl -fsS -u alice http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

### Uploads

With `--upload`, a write user (or a visitor with the PIN) can add files:

* `PUT /PATH` writes the body to the file `PATH` (`curl -T`). A new file
  gets 201, a replaced file 204. The directory of `PATH` must exist (else
  409).
* A multipart form `POST` to a directory adds each file of the form to the
  directory. A name in use gets a number (`name-1.ext`); no file is
  replaced. The listing of `--list` shows the form to a write user.
* A file goes to a hidden part file (mode 0600) first. A rename gives it
  its name when it is complete: a reader never sees a part of a file.
* `--max-upload BYTES` (default 100000000) is the most bytes of one
  request. A larger `Content-Length` gets 413 before podnet reads the
  body. A larger body with no `Content-Length` gets 413 at the limit. No
  file stays.
* A name that starts with a dot (also `..`), a link out of `--dir` and a
  read user are refused (403 or 409).

```sh
podnet serve --dir ./share --list --upload --users users --local 127.0.0.1:8080
curl -fsS -u bob -T report.pdf http://127.0.0.1:8080/inbox/report.pdf
```

The library type `podnet::origin::StaticDir` has the same rules. It also
applies them to the directory index and to the SPA index.
`podnet::feature::StaticServer::respond` gives a `StaticResponse`. Its
`body` is a reader (`std::io::Read`) that reads the file when you read
it, and `write_to` writes the head and the body. A file of any size is
served with a bounded memory.

## Git hosting

`podnet git` serves the git repositories of a root with the installed
`git` (`git http-backend`, `git upload-pack`, `git receive-pack`):

```sh
podnet git init --root ./repos app      # the bare repository ./repos/app.git
podnet git serve --root ./repos --anon-read \
  --push-user me --push-password-file ./pass   # smart HTTP through a quick tunnel
podnet git serve --root ./repos --local 127.0.0.1:8080 --ssh 127.0.0.1:2222 \
  --users users --authorized-keys ~/.ssh/authorized_keys --ingress none
podnet git serve --root ./repos --ingress relay --pair NAME \
  --authorized-keys ~/.ssh/authorized_keys     # SSH through a relay pair
podnet git urls --root ./repos          # the clone URLs and the host key
```

- A fetch needs the read role: `--anon-read`, or a user of `--users`. A
  push needs the write role: `--push-user`, a write user of `--users`, or
  a key of `--authorized-keys` (ed25519 and ECDSA only).
- `--create-on-push`: a push of a write user to a new path makes a bare
  repository there.
- The SSH host key is ed25519. podnet makes it one time
  (`git/ssh_host_ed25519_key` in the state directory, or `--host-key`).
- The operator of a relay pair clones with
  `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ProxyCommand='podnet relay connect NAME'" git clone ssh://git@NAME/REPO`.
- Limits: the quick tunnel takes at most 100 MB in one request body, so a
  larger push over HTTPS fails; a clone has no limit. A session through
  the relay ends at 64 MiB, so a larger clone or push through the relay
  fails.
- `podnet doctor` reports a missing `git`.

## Share files

```sh
podnet share --mode upload --password                 # receive files, with a PIN
podnet share --mode download --file ./report.pdf      # send one file
podnet share --file ./photos                          # send a directory as one tar
podnet share --file ./report.pdf --local 127.0.0.1:8080  # no tunnel
podnet share --mode proxy --port 3000                 # share a local port, with a PIN
podnet share --mode proxy --unix /run/api.sock        # share an HTTP unix socket, with a PIN
podnet share --mode upload --dir /tmp/inbox --stop-after --idle-secs 600
```

* Give a mode: `--mode upload` (or `--dir DIR`), `--file FILE`, `--port
  PORT` or `--unix PATH`. A bare `podnet share` is a usage error (exit 64),
  and opens no session. With `--mode upload` and no `--dir`, the files go
  to `~/Downloads/podnet` (or `~/podnet-uploads` when `~/Downloads` does not
  exist).
* The public path is `/s/<token>/`. The token has 32 random bytes, and a
  path with another token answers 404.
* `--password` adds a 6-digit PIN. The host shows the PIN. The PIN check uses
  a constant-time compare. After 10 wrong codes, no code opens the session:
  start a new one. Requests at the same time get at most 10 compares in
  total. A correct code sets the count of wrong codes to 0. After the
  unlock, the browser goes back to a path of the same site only.
* The unlock cookie has `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite=Lax`: open the
  session with `https://` (a browser does not keep a `Secure` cookie of
  plain http). An unlock POST from another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, or an
  `Origin` that is not the host) gets 403 and uses no try. A client that
  knows the URL can still use the 10 tries: the edge does not give podnet
  the address of the visitor, so the limit is for the session, not for
  each visitor.
* A locked GET or HEAD gets the PIN page with 200 (for a browser). A locked
  request with another method (an upload POST, an API call) gets the page
  with 403, and nothing is done. A wrong PIN gets 403.
* The upload limits are 512 MiB for each file, 32 files and 4 GiB in total
  for each session. A request over a limit gets 413, and no file of that
  request is saved: each file waits in a hidden `.part` file until the
  request ends. A body with no data for 60 s gets 408 and leaves no file.
* An uploaded file has mode 0600 (only the user of podnet can read it),
  with each umask.
* One upload request holds at most `--max-request` bytes (default
  100000000, the limit of the Cloudflare edge for one request body). Each
  field of the request counts, also a field with no file. A
  larger `Content-Length` gets 413 and saves nothing: podnet reads the body
  and drops it first (until its end, a pause of 5 s, or 120 s), because an
  answer before the end of the upload does not reach the visitor reliably
  through the edge. The page refuses such a selection before it sends. To
  send more, use more uploads.
* A directory in `--file` goes as one ustar stream (`DIR.tar`), with the
  rules of `serve --tar`: no dot name, no link out of the directory, no
  FIFO, socket or device.
* `--local ADDR` serves the session on a local listener (HOST:PORT,
  tcp://HOST:PORT or unix:PATH, as `serve --local`) and makes no tunnel.
  podnet prints the session URL (`url` and `path` in the `--json` line).
  It is for upload and download; proxy mode needs the tunnel.
* A download name that is not ASCII goes in `filename*=UTF-8''...` (RFC
  5987), with an ASCII `filename=`.
* `--stop-after` stops the session after the first transfer. `--idle-secs`
  stops it after a time with no activity. The idle clock starts when the
  session serves, not before the provisioning.
* Each reply of a share session has `Cache-Control: no-store`. In proxy
  mode, the replies of the local server keep their own headers.
* A download answers `If-None-Match: *` and a weak tag (`W/"..."`) with
  304.

<!-- document: docs/warp.md -->

# WARP

`podnet warp` is a WARP client (the Cloudflare WARP client, in one binary). It uses MASQUE (`CONNECT-IP` over HTTP/2) on
TCP 443. It needs no root and no TUN device.

```sh
podnet warp register                # register a device, or load the saved one
podnet warp status                  # the device and the account
podnet warp status --json           # the account record as JSON
podnet warp license <KEY>           # attach a WARP+ license key
podnet warp rotate                  # make and enrol a new MASQUE key
podnet warp delete                  # remove the device and the saved file
podnet warp probe                   # test TCP connects through the tunnel
podnet warp exit                    # the exit colo, country, address and IPv6 address
podnet warp scan --candidate 162.159.198.1   # measure front doors (TCP and TLS)
podnet warp export --out warp.conf  # a WireGuard device for other clients (UDP)
podnet warp proxy                   # local SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT proxy
podnet warp forward -L 5432=db.internal:5432   # as ssh -L, through WARP
```
