| The connect to the upstream fails, or the wait for it ends | The failure reply by its class: SOCKS5 `0x01` or `0x04`, HTTP 502 | The same closed connection |

The client cannot get a SOCKS5 error code or an HTTP status after the early reply: the reply that said
success is sent already. A client that reads `connection reset` or an empty answer cannot tell a refused
target from a closed server. The cost is this loss of the diagnosis. A program that reads the reply code to
choose its next step (a fallback to another route) must not use the option.

The flow log (`--flow-log FILE`) records the loss. An upstream that refuses a flow gives a line
`{"event":"refused","flow":N,"proto":"tcp","target":"HOST:PORT","code":C}`, with or without the option. `-v`
prints the same text.

The option does not apply to UDP, to `podssh -D` (an SSH channel cannot carry data before its open is
confirmed), to TLS early data, to `net proxy`, to `net tailscale`, to `podnet route` and to
`podnet warp proxy`.

<!-- document: docs/background.md -->

# Background runs and autostart

## Run in the background: `--detach`

```sh
podnet tunnel --port 3000 --detach --name web   # prints one JSON line, exits 0
podnet warp proxy --listen unix:/tmp/warp.sock --detach
podnet ps                                        # name, state, pid, URL or listen address
podnet logs web -f
podnet wait web                                  # the ready document again (exit 124 at --timeout)
podnet stop web                                  # or: podnet stop --all
```

`--detach` works with `tunnel`, `serve`, `share`, `demo`, `connect`,
`warp proxy`, `warp forward`, `warp tun`, `warp exec`, `relay node`,
`link listen`, `net proxy` and `net switch`. The command runs in the foreground until it
is ready: until the public URL answers, or until the listener is bound.
Then it leaves the terminal (`setsid`, SIGHUP ignored, stdin to
`/dev/null`, stdout and stderr to its log), and the start prints one JSON
document on stdout: `name`, `pid`, `log`, and `url` or `listen`. The lines
of the instance before the ready go to stderr.
The instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes. A sandbox
or a container that kills each process of its run also ends it.

* A second start with the same name and the same arguments prints the same
  document and starts nothing. Other arguments exit 69; `--replace` stops
  the instance and starts the new one.
* Without `--name`, the name is the command and a hash of its arguments.
* `--ready-timeout SECS` (default 60): after it, the start stops the
  instance and exits 124 (as `timeout`). An instance that ends before it is ready gives its
  own exit code.
* A token or a proxy password on the command line goes to the environment
  of the instance, not to its arguments or its record. The record of a
  foreground `--name` (no `--detach`) has no secret either.
* The files are in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/run/` (else `run` in the state
  directory, or `PODNET_RUN_DIR`), mode 0700: `NAME.json` (0600), `NAME.lock`
  (held while the instance runs), `NAME.secrets` (0600, only when the
  instance has a token or a proxy password: the variables that hold them)
  and `NAME.log` (0600, cut at 1 MiB; the
  part before goes to `NAME.log.1`). Each start writes a line
  `podnet: ---- start TIME pid PID name NAME ----`, then its log lines from
  the start (also the lines before the ready, which the start shows too).
  The log has no colour codes.
* A supervisor starts the instance again when it ends, with a backoff of
  1 s doubled to 30 s, but not after exit 64 or 78, and not before the first
  ready. A planned end is not restarted: `--stop-after`, `--idle-secs` and
  `--run-for` end the instance for good (a crash or a kill still restarts
  it). When the quick-tunnel service refused a provision with a
  `Retry-After` (HTTP 429), the next start waits that long (at most 1 h),
  and the run is not a quick failure. After 5 quick failures in sequence it
  runs `podnet.prev` (the binary before the last `podnet update`). A quick
  tunnel gets a new URL at a restart: `podnet ps` shows it, and the log has a
  line for it.
  `--no-restart` turns the supervisor off. `podnet stop` stops the supervisor
  and its instance.
* podnet never removes a lock file that a live process holds. When the
  record of a live instance cannot be read, `podnet ps` shows the instance
  with the state `unknown`, and `podnet stop` exits 69 and removes nothing.
  `podnet stop --all` goes on to the next instance after a failure.
* `podnet autostart add NAME --from INSTANCE` makes a detached instance start
  at boot too. It copies the arguments of the record and the secrets of
  `INSTANCE.secrets`.
* `podnet status` lists the instances.
* `--name NAME` with no `--detach` registers the process in the foreground
  (for a program that runs podnet as its child): it is not forked and not
  restarted, its stdout and stderr stay, and its log lines go to `NAME.log`
  too. `podnet ps`, `logs`, `wait` and `stop` see it. A second process with
  the name fails ("runs already"). `--replace` needs `--detach`.

## Autostart

`podnet autostart` starts a podnet command at boot and after a logout, with no
root. It uses a systemd user unit when `systemctl --user` answers, else an
`@reboot` line in the crontab. With neither, it prints the line to run at
login and exits 69.

```sh
TUNNEL_TOKEN=... podnet autostart add web -- tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
podnet autostart list
podnet autostart remove web
```

* The arguments and the variables (`TUNNEL_TOKEN`, the proxy variables,
  `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `PODNET_*`) go to private files (mode 0600) in
  `<state>/autostart/`. `--token` and a `--proxy` with a password move to
  `TUNNEL_TOKEN` and `PODNET_PROXY`. The unit, the crontab line and the
  command line of the process hold no secret.
* The unit and the line run this binary by its absolute path. A binary in
  a temporary directory is refused. The unit quotes for systemd (`%` and
  `$` are escaped), the crontab line for `sh`.
* An entry runs in the foreground under its service manager: `add`
  removes `--detach`, `--name`, `--ready-timeout` and `--no-restart`, and
  says so.
* A systemd user manager stops at logout unless linger is on:
  `loginctl enable-linger`.
* `remove` deletes only what `add` wrote (a marker line in the unit, a
  marker comment on the crontab line).
* Each program that `add` or `remove` runs has a limit of 10 s.
* With no systemd user manager and no cron, `add` exits 69. Its error text
  gives a `nohup` line: put it in a login script (for example
  `~/.profile`).

<!-- document: docs/doctor.md -->

# Checks: doctor, status, bench and bug reports

This page gives the commands that check this host and podnet: `doctor` (the path to the edge, and what
dev work can do), `pod doctor`, `net doctor`, `status`, `ports`, `bench`, `bug-report` and `agent`. Each
check gives `ok`, `fail` or `unknown`.

## `podnet doctor`

`podnet doctor` tests the path from this host to the edge, and gives `ok`,
`fail` or `unknown` for each hop (the words of `podnet net doctor` and
`podnet doctor --agent` too). In `--json`, the key is `status`; the old key
`verdict` has the same value for one release:

* the proxy of each target (the password is never printed), and the
  targets that `NO_PROXY` sends direct;
* TCP to `api.trycloudflare.com:443`, `api.cloudflareclient.com:443`, the
  edge on 7844 by name and by address, the MASQUE front door
  (`162.159.198.2:443`) and the WebSocket relay (`PODNET_RELAY`). A name is
  resolved first, with the chain of podnet: the addresses and the time, or
  the error. Each path gets up to 9 samples, 125 ms apart, in
  at most 10 s: best, median, p95, jitter and loss. A refusal (a proxy 403,
  a TCP reset) is an answer, not a loss;
* TLS on each open path: the issuer, and if the chain ends at the roots that
  podnet expects. A proxy that answers 200 and then sends no byte, and a proxy
  that terminates TLS, are named;
* names and addresses: if the proxy allows one and refuses the other;
* UDP 7844: one QUIC packet (answered, refused or unknown);
* the lane `masque_udp443`: one QUIC packet to the MASQUE front door on UDP 443.
  `ok` on any answer. `fail` on a refusal, and on silence when UDP 7844
  answers. `unknown` on silence when UDP 7844 does not answer, and when a
  proxy is set (no proxy carries UDP);
* the lane `ws_upgrade`: an HTTP/1.1 `Upgrade: websocket` request over TLS to
  the edge host on 7844, through the proxy when one is set. `ok` on `101`.
  `fail` on another status, a TLS fault or a refusal. `unknown` when no
  answer comes in twice `--timeout`. The probe adds no host: it uses the
  targets that the doctor already has;
* the clock: this host against the `Date` of the first API that answers
  TLS. More than 300 s off is `fail` (certificates and tokens fail).

Then a table of the legs `quic`, `http2`, `quic+warp` and `http2+relay`
(TCP and TLS to the relay; the relay protocol is not tried), with the
reason for each leg that cannot work, and the roads: `direct` (quic or
http2), `warp` (quic+warp) and `relay` (http2+relay). The last line,
`next:`, gives the step to take: the `podnet tunnel` command for the legs
that work, the clock to set, or the report for an issue (`next` in
`--json`). Exit 0: at least one leg can work. Exit 1: none can. `--json` gives one document; `--samples` and `--timeout`
make it shorter.

```sh
podnet doctor
podnet doctor --json | jq '.legs'
```

## What dev work can do: `podnet doctor --agent`

```sh
podnet doctor --agent           # a table and the commands to run
podnet doctor --agent --json
```

For each task (git over HTTPS and over SSH, pip, npm, cargo, go modules,
docker pull), the doctor tries three paths: `direct`, the proxy of the
environment, and a running `podnet warp up`. A TLS check is a handshake
with the public roots: `tls-intercepted` means that the chain is not
public but the CA bundle of this host (`SSL_CERT_FILE`) trusts it, so a
proxy or a gateway terminates TLS. It also tests UDP DNS to 1.1.1.1,
IPv6 and TCP on 127.0.0.1, and prints the commands: for example
`podnet warp up`, `podnet warp ssh-config`, or "nothing to do".

## Options of `podnet doctor`

* `--quick`: one sample for each path and 15 s for the whole run. A part (the two lane probes too) that does not end in time gets
  the verdict `unknown`. The JSON document keeps the same keys.
* `--samples N` (1 to 9; default 9) and `--timeout SECS` (default 3, for one connection and one TLS
  handshake) make the run shorter.
* `--relay URL` (`PODNET_RELAY`) selects the relay to test. A loopback `http://` relay is allowed.
* `--ssh-relay HOST:PORT` and `--ssh-user USER` add the row `ssh_relay`: the TCP connect, the SSH banner and
  the login of the user (the methods of [relay.md](relay.md); the key `auth_method` names the one that the relay took), with no session and no forward. With no flag, the row reads the relay of
  a running `podnet ssh-relay` instance; with no relay, the verdict is `unknown` ([relay.md](relay.md)).
* `--connect-proxy HOST:PORT` (requires `--ssh-relay`) sends the probe through this HTTP CONNECT proxy. Without
  it, the probe uses the proxy that the other commands use for the relay: `--proxy`, `PODNET_PROXY`, then the
  proxy variables, and `NO_PROXY` applies (a relay on loopback goes through the proxy too). The probe sends no
  proxy credentials. If that proxy is SOCKS5, a unix socket, a command, or has credentials, the row is `fail`
  with the reason and the probe does not dial. A proxy that answers 407 is `fail` at the stage `connect`. The
  text row names the proxy (`proxy HOST:PORT`, or `proxy none`). The JSON row has `proxy` (`http://HOST:PORT`,
  with no credentials, or `null`).
* `--json`: one document.

## The JSON document

`podnet doctor --json` prints one object with `"schema": 1`. A key is added within schema 1 and never
removed or renamed. A consumer ignores a key that it does not know. The tests pin the key sets
(`tests/doctor.rs`).

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Always 1. |
| `podnet` | The version of podnet. |
| `ok` | True when one leg is `ok`. |
| `quick` | True for a run of `--quick`. |
| `next` | The step to take now. |
| `names` | What the proxy does with names and addresses on 7844. |
| `roads` | `direct`, `warp` and `relay`, each with `verdict`, `status` and `reason`. |
| `lanes` | Seven egress lanes: `tunnel_quic`, `tunnel_http2`, `tunnel_quic_warp`, `masque_tcp443`, `masque_udp443`, `ws_upgrade` and `proxy`, each with `verdict`, `ms` and `reason`. |
| `legs` | `quic`, `http2`, `quic+warp` and `http2+relay`, each with `verdict`, `status` and `reason`. |
| `paths` | One object for each TCP path: `id`, `target`, `via`, `verdict`, `detail`, `samples` (loss, best, median, p95, jitter), `tls` and `dns`. |
| `clock`, `git`, `ssh_relay`, `proxy`, `udp` | The clock, the installed git, the SSH relay, the proxy of the run and the UDP 7844 probe. |
| `carriers` | One object for each carrier of `podnet link` ([link.md](link.md)): `carrier`, `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (the reason when the host cannot use the carrier). |

`docs/protocol.md` section 9 gives each key and its type. Section 10 is the profile for a program that
reads the document (flags, exit codes, readiness, failure causes).

## Other checks

* `podnet pod doctor [--json]` measures what the host permits for `podnet pod`: `unshare`, `/dev/net/tun`,
  `ptrace`, `seccomp` user notification, memory access of the program, netfilter in a namespace and a
  veth wire. It says whether the `netns` and the `seccomp` backend can run, the flow budget of the
  `seccomp` backend, and how much each backend holds. It exits 3 when no backend can run ([pods.md](pods.md)).
* `podnet net doctor [--json]` probes what the host permits for the virtual network: `bind` and `listen`
  for each socket family, `/dev/net/tun`, `/dev/vsock`, a C compiler for the shims, seccomp and
  capabilities, the passwd entry of this uid, UDP to the edge, `tailscaled` (`--socket PATH`; a daemon that is not `Running` is a `fail`) and the SOCKS5 listener of
  NetBird. It prints the commands that each listener allows ([networks.md](networks.md)).
* `podnet status` prints one line of JSON about this host and opens no connection: the version,
  the platform, the proxy and its source, the TLS roots in `tls_roots`, the state of the WARP identity,
  the limit of open files in `nofile`, the detached instances and `PODNET_ERROR_PROGRAM`. It has
  `"schema": 1`.
* `podnet ports [--probe] [--json]` lists the listening TCP ports of this host (Linux).
  `--probe` connects to each port and lists only those that accept. With `--json`, the others are in
  `unreachable`.
* `podnet bug-report [--doctor] [--include-link]` prints a text for a bug report: the version, `podnet status`, the
  detached instances with the end of their logs, and the names of the variables that are set. It hides
  device IDs, tunnel IDs, tokens and credentials. It opens no connection unless `--doctor` adds the JSON
  of `podnet doctor`. `--include-link` adds the dump of each link instance that runs (the verb `dump` of its control
  socket, [link.md](link.md)); an instance that does not answer is one line with the error.

## Measure a way out: `podnet bench`

`podnet bench URL` sends `GET` requests to an `http://` or `https://` URL through the way out of the
process (`--egress`, `--proxy` or the proxy variables; see [proxies.md](proxies.md)) and measures the
latency, the rate and the errors.

```sh
podnet bench https://example.com/
podnet --egress socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080 bench https://example.com/ --connections 8 --duration 20 --json
```

* `--connections N` (default 4): the requests in flight, each on its own connection.
* `--duration SECS` (default 10): the time to send requests. A request that started in time ends.
* `--timeout SECS` (default 10): the time limit of one request.
* The text output has the requests, the errors, the rate and the latency (min, p50, p95, p99, max). With
  `--json`, one document: `schema` (1), `podnet`, `url`, `connections`, `duration_s`, `requests`, `ok`,
  `errors`, `first_error`, `bytes`, `rate` and `latency_ms` (`min`, `p50`, `p95`, `p99`, `max`).

## Agent sandbox: `podnet agent`

```sh
podnet agent up --expose 3000      # test, start WARP if needed, expose port 3000
podnet agent status                # add --json for one JSON document: instances and report
podnet agent down                  # stop each part, put back each change
```

`podnet agent up` runs the checks of `podnet doctor --agent`. When direct networking does not do each task
(git over HTTPS and SSH, the registries, UDP DNS), it starts `podnet warp up` (`--persist` adds the shell
block; `--warp` starts it also when direct networking works; `--port PORT` selects the port of the WARP
proxy, default 40000). For each `--expose PORT`, it starts a detached quick tunnel (instance
`expose-PORT`), and tries `--transport relay` when the first try fails. It then runs the checks again and
prints one JSON document: `mode` (`warp` or `direct`), the paths that work for each task, the URLs, and
the commands to use (`eval "$(podnet warp env)"`, `podnet warp exec -- CMD`, `podnet warp ssh-config`).
When WARP was needed and `podnet warp up` failed, the document has `warp_error`, and the exit code is 69.
When an expose failed (its `state` in `exposed` is not `ready`), the exit code is 69 too.

<!-- document: docs/cli.md -->

# The manual, the output formats and the exit codes

This page gives the manual of podnet, the machine-readable forms (`--help --json`, `man --json`, the llms
files), the global flags, the log and JSON output, the stop signals, `--check` and the exit codes.

## Global flags

These flags work before the command (`podnet --proxy URL tunnel ...`) and after it. A flag of `podnet warp`
is not global: it goes after `warp`.

| Flag | Function |
| --- | --- |
| `--ca-file PATH` | The only TLS roots (PEM) for each connection that podnet opens ([proxies.md](proxies.md)). |
| `--proxy URL`, `--no-proxy` | The proxy of each connection, or none ([proxies.md](proxies.md)). |
| `--egress SPEC` | The way out, as a network spec ([egress.md](egress.md)). |
| `--resolve HOST=IP` | Addresses for names in place of DNS ([proxies.md](proxies.md)). |
| `-q`, `-v`, `-vv` | Warnings and errors only; debug; trace. `RUST_LOG` takes priority. |
| `--color auto\|always\|never` | Colours in the log. |
| `--log-format text\|json` | The log on stderr as text, or as one JSON object for each line. |

## The manual

`podnet man` shows the manual. It is generated from the command tree of the
binary, so it always agrees with `--help`. It needs no man(1), no groff and no
network.

```sh
podnet man                      # the whole manual, in a pager on a terminal
podnet man warp run             # one command
podnet man exit-status          # one topic: environment, files, exit-status, examples, pod
podnet man --roff > podnet.1      # a man(7) page (also a release asset)
podnet man --json               # the tables, for a program
podnet warp run --help --json   # the same JSON for one command (at each level)
podnet status                   # one JSON line about this host; no network
podnet ports --json             # the listening TCP ports, as one JSON object
podnet completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/podnet   # also zsh, fish, elvish, powershell
podnet -q tunnel ...            # warnings and errors only; -v debug, -vv trace
podnet --log-format json ...    # the log as one JSON object for each line
podnet --color never ...        # colours: auto (a terminal, no NO_COLOR), always, never
```

podnet raises the soft limit of open files (`ulimit -n`) to the hard limit at
start, at most 1048576. `podnet status` shows it in `nofile`. `warp exec`,
`warp shell`, `warp run` and `autostart run` keep the limit of the shell for
the program.

With `--json`, `podnet tunnel`, `serve`, `share` and `demo` write JSON lines on
stdout in place of the text lines. A line with `"event": "ready"` gives
`url`, `tunnel_id`, `locations` and `leg` (and `pin` for `share`). `leg` is
the edge leg that carries the tunnel: `quic`, `http2`, `quic+warp` or
`http2+relay`. The text `edge` line names it too. A line with
`"event": "verified"` comes after the fetch of the public URL. Its `dns`
field names the resolver step that resolves the public name at that time:
`system`, `doh` (public DNS resolves it, and the system resolver of this
host does not: a visitor whose resolver cached NXDOMAIN gets an error for
some seconds more), `pin` (`--resolve`) or `none`. While the fetch fails, podnet
logs the first try and each fifth try at INFO, and each try after the tenth
at WARN.

Stop signals: from the ready line (or the `ready` event) of a server
command on, SIGINT (Ctrl-C), SIGTERM and SIGHUP each start the clean
shutdown, also during the verify of the public URL and with `--run-for`.
A stop before the `verified` event gives no `verified` event. The exit
code is 0. A second signal during the shutdown stops podnet at once. Before
the ready, each signal has its default action. A detached instance ignores
SIGHUP. When the parent ignores SIGHUP (`nohup`), podnet ignores it too.

`--check` on `tunnel`, `serve`, `share` and `demo` checks the plan and stops.
It tests the flags and the config file, each origin (a connection, and the
TLS handshake for `https`; no request is sent), the files and the
directories (`--dir`, `--spa` and its `index.html`, `--file`, the upload
directory, `--warp-identity`, `--credentials-file`), `PODNET_EDGE` and the edge
legs (the `legs` row is the plan: `podnet doctor` tests the reach of each
leg). It makes no Cloudflare API call and no edge connection, opens no
listening socket and writes no file. It prints no token and no PIN. Exit 0:
each check passed. Exit 1: a check of an origin failed. Exit 78: each
failed check is a check of the configuration (`PODNET_EDGE`, the credentials
file, the roots). A bad command line (64) or a bad config file (78) stops
before the check. With `--json`, the output is one
document: `{"ok", "plan", "checks": [{"name", "status", "detail"}]}`.

```sh
podnet serve --check --dir ./site --spa
podnet tunnel --check --json --config config.yml | jq -e .ok
```

The exit codes follow sysexits.h: 64 for a bad command line, 66 when a file
that must exist is missing (the key or the allow list of the link), 69 when a
service or a network path is not available (no edge leg worked), 71 when a
file of the host cannot be used (a key file with a mode that is not 0600), 77
when a peer is not in the allow list of the link, 78 for a bad configuration
(for example `PODNET_EDGE`). 68 is for an address of a peer that does not
resolve. `podnet man exit-status` gives all of them.
The exit codes of `podnet link` are in [link.md](link.md).

`PODNET_ERROR_PROGRAM=/path/to/program` gives a JSON report of each failure
(version, system, command, exit code, the last 64 log lines) to that program
on its stdin. Credentials are masked. The program does not get
`TUNNEL_TOKEN`, the relay tokens, or a proxy variable with a user and a
password in its environment. Use it to collect failures in tests.

## Machine-readable help and the llms files

* `podnet man --json` prints the manual as one JSON object: `name`, `version`, `about`, `description`,
  `commands`, `pod_usage`, `environment`, `files`, `exit_status` and `examples`. Each entry of `commands`
  has `path`, `usage`, `about`, `long_about`, `args` and `subcommands`.
* `podnet COMMAND --help --json` prints the same entry for one command, at each level
  (`podnet route --help --json`, `podnet warp run --help --json`). Each argument has `synopsis`, `id`,
  `positional`, `required`, `repeatable`, `takes_value`, `help`, `default`, `env` and `values`.
* `podnet man --roff` prints a man(7) page. `podnet.1` is a release asset.
* `llms.txt` is an index of the commands and the documents. `llms-full.txt` holds the manual (the output of
  `podnet man --no-pager`) and the text of the documents of this repository. Both are in the root of the
  repository and are release assets. `scripts/gen-llms.py` writes them from a binary; run it after a
  change of the command tree, of the manual or of a document, and `--check` says whether they are current.
* `podnet completions SHELL` prints a completion script for `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `elvish` or `powershell`.

<!-- document: docs/library.md -->

# Library

```rust
use podnet::{Service, Tunnel};

# async fn run() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
let handle = Tunnel::quick()
    .service(Service::parse("http://127.0.0.1:8080")?)
    .ha_connections(2)
    .build()?
    .start()
    .await?;
println!("{:?}", handle.url());
handle.verify(None).await?;
handle.shutdown().await;
# Ok(())
# }
```

* `podnet::Ingress` holds ordered rules for a tunnel with more than one service.
* `podnet::warp::WarpClient` registers a device and opens a `WarpStack`, which
  has `tcp_connect` and `udp_bind` through the tunnel.
* `podnet::vnet::NetStack` is the userspace IP stack.
* `podnet::identity` keeps the Ed25519 key of an install in the state directory
  (`link-identity.key`, mode 0600) and shows its fingerprint in base32 in five
  groups of eight characters with a checksum. `AllowList` is the list of peers:
  default deny, 4096 entries at most, one fingerprint on each line. A key file
  with a wide mode exits 71, a missing key or list exits 66, and a peer that
  the list refuses exits 77 (`AllowList::check`). The seed is never printed,
  logged or put in JSON (`Identity::report`).
* `podnet::session` carries a link over the resumable layer `pod-session`. A
  link survives the loss of its carrier for 10 minutes (`RESUME_WINDOW`). A
  resume after the window fails with `ResumeExpired`, which exits 69.
* `podnet_netns::main_with_args` runs the command line of `podnet pod`. The modules
  `podnet_netns::upstream`, `socks`, `dns` and `tailscale` are also public.

<!-- document: docs/build.md -->

# Build from source

The repository is a Cargo workspace:

| Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `podnet` (root) | The CLI and the library: the edge client (provisioning, discovery, QUIC, HTTP/2, Cap'n Proto and its RPC), the service layer, WARP. |
| `crates/podnet-core` | A library: the core layer of podnet (the process, the files, the state, the reports, the supervisor). The other crates use it. |
| `crates/podnet-serve` | A library: the services of podnet (the file server, the file transfer, the gate, the ingress rules, the origins, the client of the SSH relay). It uses `podnet-core`. |
| `crates/podnet-netns` | A library: run a program with all its traffic sent through a proxy (`podnet pod`). |
| `crates/podnet-vnet` | A library: the userspace virtual network (`podnet net`) and the C sources of its `LD_PRELOAD` shims. |

## Build

```sh
cargo build --release
```

The binary is `target/release/podnet`. Rust
1.99 or newer is necessary. The build takes the `pod-*` crates from the
git repository `PodUtils/podcrates` (by tag), so it needs access to
GitHub.

A static binary has no run-time dependency on the C library of the host:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl=clang cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
```

The `LD_PRELOAD` shims need a C compiler at run time (`cc`, `gcc` or
`clang`). The other commands do not.

## Features

The default build has no optional feature. An optional carrier or service of
the link sits behind a Cargo feature of the `podnet` crate:

| Feature | Holds | Entry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quic` | The QUIC carrier. | T-273 |
| `s3` | The object-storage carrier. | T-279 |
| `icmp` | The ICMP echo carrier. | T-282 |
| `ss` | The Shadowsocks service. | T-294 |
| `trojan` | The Trojan service. | T-295 |
| `c-abi` | The C ABI. | T-304 |
| `portable` | The portable subset. It takes code away. | T-305 |
| `full` | `quic`, `s3`, `icmp`, `ss`, `trojan` and `c-abi`. It does not hold `portable`. | T-311 |

```sh
cargo build --release --features quic,icmp   # two optional carriers
cargo test --workspace --features full       # what the CI job features runs
```

* `full` is for CI. No flag at run time turns a feature on: a binary cannot
  run code that it was not built with.
* A carrier whose feature is off stays in the registry. `podnet link carriers`
  lists it with the reason `not built: the feature NAME is off (build with
  --features NAME)`, `podnet doctor` shows it as `unknown`, and a command
  that names it (`--carrier NAME`) exits 69 with the same reason. In a
  `--features` build, a carrier whose code is not in the tree yet says so.
* The static musl build of the release set uses the default features. Build
  a feature on every target of the release set before it joins that set.
* `podnet::build_features` is the list (`OPTIONAL`, `FULL`), `built(NAME)`,
  `enabled()` and `require(NAME)` (the gate of a command: exit 69 with the
  feature name).

## Fuzz

`fuzz/` has a libFuzzer target for each parser of bytes from the network
(Cap'n Proto, the RPC of the edge, capsules, proxy URLs and answers, SRV
and DoH, ACL rules, ingress rules, YAML, HTTP/2 headers, vnet frames, the
request head to the origin). It
needs a nightly toolchain and glibc. `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` runs each
target each week. A crash input becomes a unit test before the fix.

```sh
cargo +stable install cargo-fuzz --locked --version 0.13.1
cd fuzz
cargo +nightly-2026-10-15 run --bin seed -- corpus
cargo +nightly-2026-10-15 fuzz run capnp_message corpus/capnp_message -- -max_total_time=60 -malloc_limit_mb=64
```

`cargo test` runs each target on its seeds and on 2000 fixed mutations
(`fuzzing::tests::each_target_survives_mutations`).

<!-- document: docs/protocol.md -->

# Edge protocol and WARP protocol

This document gives the wire behaviour that `podnet` uses. The reference is
`cloudflared` (`github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared`). File names in this
document are paths in that repository.

## 1. Quick-tunnel provisioning

A quick tunnel starts with one HTTPS request
(`cmd/cloudflared/tunnel/quick_tunnel.go`):

```text
POST https://api.trycloudflare.com/tunnel
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: cloudflared/<version>
```

The body is empty. A good answer is:

```json
{"success":true,"result":{
  "id":"<uuid>","name":"qt-...","hostname":"<random>.trycloudflare.com",
  "account_tag":"<hex>","secret":"<base64, 32 bytes>"},"errors":[]}
```

`id`, `account_tag` and `secret` are the `TunnelAuth` credentials for the
registration. `--service-url` changes the endpoint. The request goes on TCP
443 and uses `HTTPS_PROXY` when it is set.

`podnet` does not log the answer body when it cannot decode it, because the body
contains the tunnel secret.

## 2. Edge discovery

The edge addresses come from the SRV record
`_v2-origintunneld._tcp.argotunnel.com`. The targets are
`region1.v2.argotunnel.com` and `region2.v2.argotunnel.com`, port 7844
(`edgediscovery/allregions`).

`podnet` tries these sources in sequence:

1. DNS over HTTPS (the JSON API of `cloudflare-dns.com`). This works on hosts
   that have no DNS resolver but have HTTPS egress.
2. The system resolver, then DNS over TLS.
3. A static list of edge addresses.

`PODNET_EDGE=ip:port,ip:port` replaces discovery.

## 3. Transports

| Protocol | Socket | TLS SNI | ALPN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QUIC | UDP 7844 | `quic.cftunnel.com` | `argotunnel` |
| HTTP/2 | TCP 7844 | `h2.cftunnel.com` | none |

* The SNI and the ALPN of QUIC are different strings. If the ALPN value is
  sent as the SNI, the handshake completes key derivation and then stops.
* The edge certificate chains to Cloudflare roots that are not in public
  trust stores. The roots are the fact `roots` of the edge of `pod-services`
  (PodUtils/podcrates), the certificates of `src/cloudflare/cf-edge-roots.pem`
  (from `tlsconfig/cloudflare_ca.go`). Without them, TLS fails with
  `UnknownIssuer`.
* Port 443 of the edge does not serve the tunnel service: TLS there is
  TLS 1.2, and its chain does not end at the edge roots (section 6). So
  podnet uses 7844 only, and carries the edge on TCP 443 inside WARP
  (section 5.3).

### 3.1 QUIC

The first bidirectional stream that `podnet` opens is the control stream. It has
no preamble. It carries capnp RPC: `podnet` calls
`RegistrationServer.registerConnection(auth, tunnelId, connIndex, options)`
(`connection/quic_connection.go`, `tunnelrpc/registration_client.go`). The edge
opens each later stream for one visitor request.

`podnet` also serves a `CloudflaredServer` bootstrap object on the control
stream. The edge uses it as a liveness check. Without it, the edge marks the
tunnel offline and visitors get HTTP 530.

Registration features (`ClientInfo.features`): podnet sends the default
list of cloudflared 2026.10.7 (`features/features.go`), which is
`support_datagram_v2` only (`schema::FEATURES`). cloudflared 2026.10.7
removes `serialized_headers`, `quick_reconnects`, `allow_remote_config`,
`support_quic_eof` and `management_logs` before it sends the list
(TUN-10904: the edge supports them with no flag), and also
`support_datagram_v3` and `support_datagram_v3_1`. podnet does not send
`postquantum` (it uses a classical key exchange, section 6) or
`support_datagram_v3_2` (it carries no UDP or ICMP datagram of a visitor).
The answers of HTTP/2 always carry the serialized header (section 3.2).

cloudflared makes one connection for a quick tunnel (`ha-connections` is
set to 1 in `quick_tunnel.go`) and four for a named tunnel. podnet makes two
by default for both (`--ha-connections`, 1 to 8). The extra connections are
for redundancy: each one registers with the edge, and the edge chooses the
connection of each visitor request. One request (one stream) uses one
connection, so `--ha-connections` does not make one transfer faster; it can
let more requests run at the same time on more connections.

Each connection starts at another region, as in cloudflared: connection 0
(and 2) dials the addresses of `region1` first, connection 1 (and 3) the
addresses of `region2`. A fault of one region then does not hit each
connection. IPv4 addresses stay before IPv6 addresses.

### 3.2 HTTP/2

`connection/http2.go`. On the TLS connection, the edge is the HTTP/2 client and
`podnet` is the HTTP/2 server. The edge opens a stream for each request.
`podnet` classifies each stream from its headers, in this order:

| Condition | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `Cf-Cloudflared-Proxy-Connection-Upgrade: update-configuration` | configuration push |
| `Cf-Cloudflared-Proxy-Connection-Upgrade: websocket` | WebSocket |
| `Cf-Cloudflared-Proxy-Src` is not empty | TCP stream |
| `Cf-Cloudflared-Proxy-Connection-Upgrade: control-stream` | control stream |
| all other requests | HTTP |

* Control stream: `podnet` sends status 200 and keeps the stream open. The
  request body and the response body carry the same capnp RPC as on QUIC.
* HTTP: the visitor headers are plain HTTP/2 headers. `podnet` changes the
  request into the `ConnectRequest` of section 4 and serves it with the same
  service layer as QUIC.
* Response: the origin headers go in one header,
  `cf-cloudflared-response-headers`, as `base64(name):base64(value)` pairs with
  `;` between them (raw standard base64, no padding). The HTTP/2 rules for
  header values do not apply to that header. `content-length` is also sent as
  a plain header. `cf-cloudflared-response-meta: {"src":"origin"}` tells the
  edge that the origin answered. Status 101 becomes 200, because HTTP/2 has no
  101.
* WebSocket: `podnet` adds `Connection: Upgrade` and `Upgrade: websocket` for the
  origin, because HTTP/2 has no upgrade headers.
* Configuration push: `podnet` answers `{"lastAppliedVersion":N,"err":null}`
  with the version of the push. A push of more than 64 KiB, or a push that
  does not end in 30 seconds, gets `{"lastAppliedVersion":-1,"err":"..."}`.
* Limits: the HTTP/2 handshake after TLS has a time limit of 10 seconds.
  The edge can open 256 streams at the same time, as on QUIC.

`tools/check-header-oracle.sh` compares the header encoding of `podnet` with the
Go function `SerializeHeaders` of cloudflared.

### 3.3 Leg order

`--protocol auto --transport auto` tries QUIC, then HTTP/2, then QUIC through
WARP (section 5). The attempts are real registrations, in a staggered race
(`crates/podnet-core/src/race.rs`, `--leg-failover staggered`, the default):

* The next leg starts when the leg before has not registered in 2 seconds,
  or at once when it fails. A filtered port does not answer, so a host that
  drops UDP and TCP 7844 starts WARP after about 4 seconds, not 16.
* The first leg that registers stays. When two legs register in the same
  turn, the earlier leg of the order stays. Each other leg that registered
  gets the unregister call, and then its connection closes. The legs that
  still run are cancelled.

`--leg-failover serial` starts a leg only after the one before failed. When
another leg can follow, an attempt has the time limit of the budgets of its
leg (`attempt_limit` in `src/tunnel.rs`): 3 tries of the registration, each
with the limits of its steps, and 5 seconds at most between two tries.

| Leg | One try | Time limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quic` | QUIC handshake 10 s, registration 30 s | 130 s |
| `http2`, `http2+relay` | TCP, TLS and HTTP/2 handshake 10 s each, control stream and registration 30 s each | 280 s |
| `quic+warp` | | no limit |

A try over more than one edge address can take longer than one try of the
table. The time limit then stops it, and the next leg starts.

UDP (`PODNET_UDP`, `crates/podnet-core/src/udp.rs`): with `probe` (the default) and
`--protocol auto`, podnet sends one QUIC packet with a reserved version (RFC
9000 section 15) to an edge address on UDP 7844 while the quick tunnel is
provisioned. The result is answered (a datagram came back), refused (the send
failed, or an ICMP error came back on the connected socket) or unknown (no
answer in 150 ms). Only refused removes the QUIC leg; unknown and answered
keep the order. A bind alone never gives answered. `PODNET_UDP=off` removes the
QUIC leg; `PODNET_UDP=on` sends no probe. `podnet net doctor` sends the same
packet with a deadline of 3 s.

The stagger is not a probe: each leg is a full attempt on its own port and
protocol. `podnet` does not probe TCP 7844 to select a leg, because a firewall
can close TCP 7844 and keep UDP 7844 open. Inside a leg, the HTTP/2 dial
starts the next edge address 250 ms after the one before (RFC 8305).

### 3.4 HTTP/2 through a WebSocket relay

`--transport relay` (`src/ws_relay.rs`) has one leg, `http2+relay`. It is
the HTTP/2 leg of section 3.2, with a different TCP dial:

1. TCP to the relay on port 443 (through `HTTPS_PROXY` when it is set),
   then TLS with ALPN `http/1.1` and the public roots.
2. A WebSocket upgrade to `wss://RELAY/connect/IP/7844`, with the token in
   the `X-Relay-Token` header. IP is an IPv4 edge address of discovery.
3. Binary frames carry the TCP bytes both ways. podnet sends frames of 16 KiB
   or less; the relay writes at most 64 KiB to a Worker socket in one call.
   An empty frame from the relay is a keepalive; podnet skips it.
4. In the WebSocket: TLS to the edge (SNI `h2.cftunnel.com`, the edge
   roots), then HTTP/2 as in section 3.2.

The token: `PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN`, or `POST /v1/mint` with the body `{}`, which
gives `{token, expires}`. A minted token is minted again when it has less
than 10 minutes. A 403 for a minted token mints a new one one time. A 403
that names the ALLOW list is a policy refusal: a new token does not help.
A minted token is kept in `relay-token-HOST.json` (mode 0600) in the state
directory, so the next process does not mint again.

The hosts: `--relay` (or `PODNET_RELAY`) takes one URL or a comma list.
`pod-relay` of PodUtils/podcrates keeps the hosts, the tokens and the pool
(`src/ws_relay.rs` is the glue). Each deployment of a list gets its own
token. The default relay takes the first 3 hosts of its pool as alternates
(`MAX_ALTERNATES` of `pod-relay`): the `pool[].host` names of
`/relays.json`, read after a mint and kept for 7 days in
`relay-pool-HOST.json`. Until a pool is cached, the default relay uses the
first 3 hosts of its seed. The seed holds 6 hosts in different regions
(`pod-services`). Another relay host has no alternates. A connect tries the
first host, then the next host after 2 s, or at once after a failure. A
refused fixed token or a policy refusal stops the hosts that did not start:
another host gives the same answer. On 2026-11-04 each of the 37 hosts of the
pool reached `198.41.192.167:7844` (`/trace?target=`, road `vpc`).

Limits of `tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev` (podssh measured them; the relay sets
them, and they can change):

| Limit | Value | Effect on the leg |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No payload | 180 s | The HTTP/2 PING each 30 s is payload. |
| Bytes of a session | 64 MiB, both directions, TLS included | At 60 MiB, podnet takes no new stream on the connection and connects a replacement. The open streams go on. |
| Time of a session | 12 h | The same at 11 h 30 min. |
| MASQUE through the relay | the same budget | At 60 MiB or 11 h 30 min, a new MASQUE session takes the new flows. The open flows go on in the old session; it closes after 90 s (`warp::live::RENEW_DRAIN`). |
| Egress | IPv4 TCP; Cloudflare addresses through the Workers VPC route | No QUIC; IPv6 edge addresses are skipped. |

podssh measured TLS to `region1.v2.argotunnel.com:7844` through this relay
(GitHub Actions run 41072705691). The live check of podnet registers a quick
tunnel through it with UDP and TCP 7844 dropped on the host. Measured
2026-11-01 (live run 41303368779): `http2+relay` registered at ord02 in
743 ms, the second connection registered at ord02, and the public URL
answered 200.

## 4. Stream framing (QUIC)

A visitor stream starts with a 6-byte signature (`0A 36 CD 12 A1 3E`), the
2-byte version `01`, and a capnp `ConnectRequest`:

* `dest`: the URL (HTTP and WebSocket) or `host:port` (TCP).
* `type`: `http`, `websocket` or `tcp`.
* `metadata`: `HttpMethod`, `HttpHost`, and one `HttpHeader:<Name>` entry for
  each header value.

`podnet` answers with the same preamble and a capnp `ConnectResponse` (`error`,
`metadata`). After that, the stream is a byte pipe. The schemas are in
`src/cloudflare/schemas/`. `src/cloudflare/capnp.rs` implements the Cap'n
Proto encoding and `src/cloudflare/rpc.rs` the RPC subset (section 3.1).

In the response metadata, the status is the entry `HttpStatus`. Each header
must be an entry `HttpHeader:<Name>`. The edge drops a key without the prefix.
Then it makes its own chunked framing and sends no origin headers.

## 5. WARP

### 5.1 Registration

The API is `https://api.cloudflareclient.com/v0a5641`. All calls use the
headers `User-Agent: WARP for Android` and `CF-Client-Version: a-6.38.9-5641`.
After a dial, TLS or 5xx failure, podnet sends the call again to the second
name of the API, `https://api.devices.cloudflare.com` (it answered
`GET /reg/{id}` of an unknown device with the same 404 on 2026-11-04).
`PODNET_WARP_API=https://HOST[:PORT]` sets the one base to use.

| Call | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /reg` | Make a device. The answer has the device `id` and a bearer `token`. |
| `PATCH /reg/{id}` | Enrol a P-256 key (X.509 SPKI, base64), `key_type: secp256r1`, `tunnel_type: masque`. |
| `GET /reg/{id}` | Read the device. |
| `GET /reg/{id}/account` | Read the account: type, WARP+ state, quota. |
| `PUT /reg/{id}/account` | Attach a license key: `{"license":"..."}`. |
| `DELETE /reg/{id}` | Remove the device. |

Only the answer to `POST /reg` has the token. `podnet` keeps it in the saved
identity file, because the other calls need it. A key rotation is a new
`PATCH /reg/{id}` with a new key.

The device record gives the MASQUE endpoint (for example `162.159.198.2:443`),
the public key of the endpoint, and the tunnel addresses (`172.16.0.2` and an
IPv6 address in `2606:4700:110::/48`).

### 5.2 MASQUE session

* TLS to the endpoint on TCP 443, SNI `consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com`,
  ALPN `h2`. The client certificate is self-signed with the enrolled P-256 key.
  `podnet` checks the server key against the key in the device record.
* One HTTP/2 extended `CONNECT` to `https://cloudflareaccess.com` with
  `cf-connect-proto: cf-connect-ip`.
* The DATA frames of that stream carry capsules (RFC 9297). Each IP packet is
  one capsule of type 0. The value is the bare IP packet, with no context
  ID before it (RFC 9484 puts a context ID of 0 there). podnet writes and
  reads no context ID (`capsule::tests::a_data_capsule_has_no_context_id`).
  The tunnel MTU is 1280.
* The request headers: `cf-connect-proto: cf-connect-ip`,
  `capsule-protocol: ?1`, `pq-enabled: false` and an empty `user-agent`.
  The front door accepts them (measured, podssh issue 63, a run of podnet).
* The server certificate is not publicly trusted: its root is
  `CN=2024-02-27 Self-Signed Root, O=Cloudflare, Inc.` (measured, live run
  41268348982, `podnet doctor`). Its key is byte for byte the SPKI of the
  `PATCH` answer, which is what podnet pins (measured, podssh issue 63).
* A client certificate that does not match the enrolled key gives a TLS
  alert, not an HTTP status (measured, podssh issue 63). podnet reports it as
  "TLS alert from the peer" (`hop::tls_text`).
* The `PATCH` answer lists the endpoint ports
  `[443, 500, 1701, 4500, 4443, 8443, 8095]` (measured, podssh issue 63).
  podnet uses 443 only (`register::MASQUE_PORT`).
* The newer L4 proxy mode of the front door is HTTP/3 only (read, podssh
  issue 63). podnet uses CONNECT-IP over HTTP/2.
* `smoltcp` owns the tunnel address and runs TCP and UDP on it. This is
  `podnet::warp::WarpStack`.

### 5.3 The edge through WARP

`podnet::warp::quic::endpoint` makes a `noq::Endpoint` whose UDP socket is a
UDP socket of the `WarpStack` (`pod_quic::queued::QueuedDatagrams` of
PodUtils/podcrates). The QUIC connection to the edge (UDP 7844) thus
goes inside the MASQUE session. The host opens only TCP 443.

### 5.4 Limits

* The WARP service limits new devices (`POST /reg`) for each address:
  HTTP 429 with error 1015 (observed after about 10 in 90 minutes).
* A destination sees an egress address of Cloudflare, not the address of
  the device. One MASQUE session keeps one egress address; a new session
  gets a new one (measured by a tester, issue 183). `--session-max-age`
  renews the session on purpose.

* A proxy that terminates TLS (and makes a new TLS connection with its own CA)
  cannot carry the MASQUE session, because the session needs the client
  certificate and the pinned server key. The registration calls still work
  through such a proxy.
* The WARP proxy of `podnet` (`podnet warp proxy`) carries TCP (SOCKS5 and HTTP
  `CONNECT`) and UDP (SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE). It resolves names through the
  tunnel. The UDP relay socket of an association is on `127.0.0.1`. When the
  proxy cannot open it, the reply is `0x01` (general failure).
* A host that refuses UDP on `127.0.0.1` uses the UDP association in the
  stream: the SOCKS5 command `0x83`
  (`pod_proxy::udp::CMD_UDP_IN_STREAM`) in place of `0x03`. The reply
  has no relay address. Each datagram then goes on the control connection
  as a frame: a length of 2 bytes (big-endian), then the datagram with its
  SOCKS5 UDP header (RFC 1928 section 7). The answers come back the same
  way. `podnet warp run --backend seccomp` and `podnet pod` use it; the unix
  socket of `podnet warp up` serves it.
* A name in a UDP datagram (ATYP 3) is resolved once for each association,
  with an A query through the tunnel; AAAA only when there is no A record.
  A DNS query through the tunnel is sent again after 1.2 s, in a time limit
  of 5 s.

## 6. Edge, measured

Each row has a mark: **measured** (a command ran, with its date and run),
**read** (from the source of cloudflared 2026.10.7 or from a document) or
**inferred**. The tool is `PodUtils/podcrates:scripts/services/edge-facts.sh`
(from the tag v0.14.0); the workflow `services.yml` of
podcrates runs it each day and by hand (input `measure`). The rows below are
from run 41268348982 (2026-11-01, a GitHub runner, ubuntu-24.04), address
198.41.192.107. Its exit code is 1 when one of the two facts that podnet needs
is not true (the rows marked *need*).

| Fact | Result | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SRV `_v2-origintunneld._tcp.argotunnel.com` | `1 1 7844 region1.v2.argotunnel.com.` and `2 1 7844 region2.v2.argotunnel.com.` | measured |
| Addresses of `region1.v2.argotunnel.com` | 10: 198.41.192.7, .27, .37, .47, .57, .67, .77, .107, .167, .227 | measured |
