| Latency from the runner to the edge, TCP | best 6.2 ms, median 7.2 ms (`podnet doctor`, 9 samples) | measured |
| cloudflared and `HTTPS_PROXY` | Two requests for a proxy for the edge, cloudflare/cloudflared#350 and #1025, are closed (2023-09-05). podnet uses the proxy for each TCP connection (section 1, `src/egress.rs`) | read |
| The prechecks of cloudflared | They use the name `probe.cftunnel.com` and test DNS, QUIC, TCP and TLS to both regions, and `api.cloudflare.com:443` | read (podssh design notes, cloudflared 2026.10.6) |

`podnet doctor` measures the same path on any host, through its proxy.

## 7. Limits of quick tunnels

From the Cloudflare page
[Quick Tunnels](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/)
(read 2026-11-01):

* Quick tunnels are for testing and development. For production, use a
  named tunnel (`--token` or `--config` with `credentials-file:`).
* No uptime guarantee.
* At most 200 requests in flight for each quick tunnel. More get `429`.
* No Server-Sent Events (SSE). An event stream can arrive in bursts, or at
  its end.

The provision service (`api.trycloudflare.com`) also limits the
provisions of each address. Observed (issue 182): after 5 to 7
provisions in 12 to 70 minutes, the service answers `429` (error 1015)
with a `Retry-After`. The wait is a fixed expiry: a new request does not
make it longer. podnet waits at most 300 s for one provision (with
`--detach`, at most `--ready-timeout` for the first start), then exits 75
with `retry_after_s` in the error report. A script needs its own loop. A
supervisor of `--detach` waits the `Retry-After` (at most 1 h) before its
next start. Each restart of a quick tunnel uses one provision.

cloudflared makes one edge connection for a quick tunnel (section 3.1).

## 8. Terms

These documents apply. This section gives facts, not legal advice.

* Quick tunnels: the disclaimer of cloudflared 2026.10.7
  (`cmd/cloudflared/tunnel/quick_tunnel.go`) says that account-less
  tunnels "are subject to the Cloudflare Online Services Terms of Use
  (https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/)", and that Cloudflare may
  investigate the use of tunnels for violations of those terms.
* WARP: the Application Terms of the WARP client license "the
  Application", and forbid reverse engineering of it. Cloudflare may
  "block certain kinds of usage" (read, podssh design notes). podnet is a
  separate program: it contains no code of the WARP application, and it
  uses the public registration API of section 5.1.

## 9. `podnet doctor --json`, schema 1

`podnet doctor --json` prints one JSON object. The key `schema` is 1. Within
schema 1, a key is added, and never removed or renamed. A consumer ignores a
key that it does not know. The test `doctor_json_keys_are_fixed`
(`tests/doctor.rs`) pins the key sets.

`--quick` makes one sample for each path and ends the run in 15 s. A part that
does not end in time gets the verdict `unknown` and the reason `no answer in
the time limit of --quick`. The keys stay the same.

The verdict words are `ok`, `fail` and `unknown`. The key `status` has the
same word as `verdict` in each object that has both. In `udp`, `verdict` is
one of `answered`, `refused` and `unknown`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | number | Always 1. |
| `podnet` | string | The version of podnet. |
| `ok` | bool | True when one leg is `ok`. |
| `quick` | bool | True for a run of `--quick`. |
| `next` | string | The step to take now. |
| `names` | string or null | What the proxy does with names and addresses on 7844. |
| `roads` | array | One object for each road (`direct`, `warp`, `relay`). |
| `lanes` | object | The seven egress lanes (below). |
| `legs` | array | One object for each leg (`quic`, `http2`, `quic+warp`, `http2+relay`). |
| `paths` | array | One object for each TCP path (the hops). |
| `clock` | object | The clock against the `Date` of an API. |
| `git` | object | The installed git. |
| `ssh_relay` | object | The SSH relay of `podnet ssh-relay`. |
| `carriers` | array | One object for each carrier of `podnet link`. |
| `proxy` | object | The proxy of the run. |
| `udp` | object | The UDP 7844 probe. |

Each object of `roads` has `road`, `verdict`, `status` and `reason` (strings).
Each object of `legs` has `leg`, `verdict`, `status` and `reason` (strings).

Each object of `paths`:

| Key | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | string |
| `target` | string (`host:port`) |
| `via` | string or null (the proxy) |
| `verdict`, `status`, `detail` | string |
| `samples` | object: `sent` and `answered` (numbers), `loss` (number, 0 to 1), `best_ms`, `median_ms`, `p95_ms` and `jitter_ms` (number or null) |
| `tls` | object or null: `verdict`, `status`, `issuer` (string or null), `detail` |
| `dns` | object or null: `addresses` (strings) and `ms`, or `error` |

* `clock`: `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (strings), `skew_s` (number or
  null).
* `git`: `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (strings), `version` (string or
  null).
* `ssh_relay`: `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (strings); `relay` (string
  or null: `HOST:PORT`), `user` (string or null) and `source` (string or
  null: `flag` or `instance NAME`); `connect_ms` and `total_ms` (number or
  null); `banner` (string or null: the SSH identification of the relay);
  `auth` (bool or null: the relay accepted the user). The probe opens no
  session and asks for no forward. The relay comes from `--ssh-relay
  HOST:PORT` with `--ssh-user USER`, else from the first running
  `ssh-relay` instance (`podnet ps`). With neither, `verdict` is `unknown`
  and `detail` is `no SSH relay is given`. A stage that fails has `fail`
  and the stage in `detail` (`connect`, `banner`, `handshake` or `auth`). A
  stage with no answer in three times `--timeout` has `unknown`.
* `carriers`: one object for each carrier of the registry, in its order: `carrier`, `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (strings).
  `ok` means that the host can use the carrier. `fail` means that it cannot, and `detail` gives the reason of `available()`.
* `proxy`: `url` (string or null), `credentials` (bool or null), `direct`
  (strings), `text` (string).
* `udp`: `target`, `verdict`, `status` and `detail` (strings).

### Lanes

`lanes` has exactly the seven keys below. Each value is an object with
`verdict` (`ok`, `fail` or `unknown`), `ms` (number or null: the best TCP
sample of the lane, or the answer time of a probe) and `reason` (string).

| Lane | Source | `ms` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tunnel_quic` | the leg `quic` | null |
| `tunnel_http2` | the leg `http2` | the path `edge-address` |
| `tunnel_quic_warp` | the leg `quic+warp` | the MASQUE path |
| `masque_tcp443` | the path `masque`, or `masque-v6` when only it works | the same path |
| `masque_udp443` | one QUIC packet to the MASQUE endpoint on UDP 443: `ok` on any answer (`ms` is the time); `fail` on a refusal, and on silence when UDP 7844 answers; `unknown` on silence when it does not, and with a proxy (no proxy carries UDP) | the answer time, else null |
| `ws_upgrade` | an HTTP/1.1 `Upgrade: websocket` request over TLS to the edge host on 7844, through the proxy when one is set: `ok` on `101`; `fail` on another status, a TLS fault or a refusal; `unknown` on no answer in twice `--timeout` | the time to the status line when `ok`, else null |
| `proxy` | the paths that go through a proxy: `ok` when one works, `fail` when each fails, else `unknown` (`no proxy is set` without a proxy) | the best of the working paths |

## 10. The connector profile

A connector is a program that starts `podnet tunnel` and reads its output.
This section lists what such a program can rely on. The newest signed
release that has the profile is v0.4.0-beta.3.

The rule: within a minor version (0.4.x), a change to the profile only adds.
A flag, an exit code, a JSON key or a value word is never removed or renamed.
A consumer ignores a key that it does not know. The test
`connector_profile_is_pinned` (`tests/cli/profile.rs`) checks the lists below
against the binary and against this file. The test `the_ready_keys_are_fixed`
(`src/cli/cmd/run.rs`) pins the keys of the ready line.

### Flags of `podnet tunnel`

`--auth-password-file`, `--auth-user`, `--ca-file`, `--check`, `--color`,
`--config`, `--credentials-file`, `--detach`, `--egress`, `--forward`,
`--ha-connections`, `--hello-world`, `--help`, `--http-host-header`, `--json`,
`--leg-failover`, `--log-format`, `--name`, `--no-proxy`, `--no-restart`,
`--no-tls-verify`, `--no-verify`, `--port`, `--protocol`, `--proxy`, `--qr`,
`--quiet`, `--ready-timeout`, `--relay`, `--replace`, `--resolve`,
`--run-for`, `--service-url`, `--strip-accept-encoding`, `--tcp`, `--token`,
`--token-file`, `--transport`, `--unix`, `--url`, `--user-agent`, `--verbose`,
`--warp-identity`.

### Exit codes

The list is `podnet man exit-status`. An error with no class exits 1.

| Code | Name |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | `success` |
| 1 | `failure` |
| 3 | `no-backend` |
| 64 | `usage` |
| 66 | `no-input` |
| 68 | `no-host` |
| 69 | `unavailable` |
| 71 | `os-error` |
| 75 | `tempfail` |
| 77 | `no-permission` |
| 78 | `config` |
| 124 | `timeout` |

### Readiness

podnet has no HTTP endpoint `/ready` and no metrics listener (`--metrics` is
refused with exit 64). A connector reads the ready line instead. With
`--json`, `tunnel` prints it on stdout when the tunnel is up. With
`--detach`, the same data is the ready document: the last line of stdout of
the start, and the key `ready` of an instance in `ps --json`.

The ready line has `event` (always `ready`), `schema` (1), `podnet` (the
version), `url` (string or null), `tunnel_id` (string), `locations` (array of
strings) and `leg` (string). With `--forward` it also has `forward` (string
or null) and `forward_path` (string).

The ready document has `url` (string or null), `verified` (bool), `tunnel_id`,
`locations` and `leg`. It has `unverified` (string) when the check of the
public URL did not finish, and `forward` and `forward_path` as the ready line
does.

### `podnet ps --json`

One object with `schema` (1), `podnet` (the version), `dir` (string: the run
directory) and `instances` (array). Each instance has these keys:

| Key | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | string |
| `state` | string (`starting` or `ready`) |
| `pid` | number |
| `supervisor` | number or null |
| `command` | string |
| `args` | array of strings |
| `cwd` | string |
| `started` | number (Unix seconds) |
| `restarts` | number |
| `log` | string (a path) |
| `ready` | object or null (the ready document) |

### `podnet doctor --json`

Section 9. The test `doctor_json_keys_are_fixed` (`tests/doctor.rs`) pins it.

## Failure causes

The error line of podnet names the hop that failed, and a second line says
what may help. The failure report (`PODNET_ERROR_PROGRAM`) has the hop in
`hop`. The text of a peer (a proxy reply, an edge reason) is kept, with no
control characters.

| Hop | Example cause | podnet does | What may help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `proxy` | `403 Forbidden: not on the egress allowlist`, 407 with NTLM | Stops the attempt; another leg can follow | Fix the proxy URL or its allow-list; `--no-proxy` |
| `dns` | No resolver answers, DoH blocked | Tries the system resolver, then DoH by IP address | `--resolve HOST=IP`; `socks5h://` |
| `tls` | `UnknownIssuer`, `TLS alert from the peer: HandshakeFailure`, an expired certificate | Stops the attempt | `--ca-file` for a TLS-inspecting proxy; check the clock |
| `edge-register` | A refusal with `should_retry = false` (bad token, deleted tunnel) | Stops the leg; does not retry | Check the token, or use a quick tunnel |
| `edge-register` | A refusal with `retry_after` | Retries after `retry_after` (1 s to 300 s) | Nothing |
| `edge-stream` | No PING answer, GOAWAY, a lost connection | Connects again at once, then with backoff and jitter, with no limit | `--transport warp` on a host with only TCP 443 |
| `origin` | Connection refused | Answers the visitor with 502 | Start the origin; check `--url` |

`scripts/soak.sh` runs N quick tunnels end to end, keeps one log for each
trial, and prints the failure rate.

<!-- document: docs/virtual-network.md -->

# Virtual network (`podnet net`, `podnet::vnet`)

The virtual network gives programs IPv4 and IPv6 addresses on a host where the
kernel refuses `AF_INET` and `AF_INET6` binds. It needs no network namespace,
no TUN device and no capability. It needs only `AF_UNIX`, including the
abstract namespace.

Use `podnet net doctor` to see what the host permits.

## 1. Parts

| Part | Module | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shim | `crates/podnet-vnet/shim/podnet-vnet.c`, `vnet::shim` | An `LD_PRELOAD` library. It changes `AF_INET` sockets into `AF_UNIX` abstract sockets. |
| Stack | `vnet::stack` | A `smoltcp` TCP/IP stack. It owns the virtual addresses. |
| Link | `vnet::device`, `vnet::framing` | The packet queues of the stack, and the framing for a byte stream. |
| Proxy | `vnet::proxy` | A SOCKS5 and HTTP `CONNECT` front door into the stack. |
| Switch | `vnet::switch` | A hub that connects stacks, and the fault injector. |
| Resolver | `vnet::dns` | A DNS server at the gateway for virtual names. |
| Policy | `vnet::policy` | Allow and deny rules, applied at connect time. |
| Capture | `vnet::record` | pcap capture and replay of the link. |
| Control | `vnet::control` | The protocol between the shim and the stack. |

## 2. Addresses

| Address | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `10.66.0.0/24`, `fd00:66::/64` | The virtual subnets. |
| `10.66.0.1` | The gateway. The virtual resolver listens on port 53. |
| `10.66.0.2` to `10.66.0.254` | Stacks and programs. |

The kernel does not see these addresses. `podnet net addresses` prints the plan.

## 3. Shim

Build the shim and start a program with it:

```sh
podnet net shim --out /tmp/podnet-vnet --log
LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/podnet-vnet/libpodnet-vnet.so ./server
```

### 3.1 Address translation

An IP endpoint becomes an abstract socket name:

```text
\0podnet-vnet/<family>/<address>/<port>

10.66.0.2:8080   ->  \0podnet-vnet/4/10.66.0.2/8080
[fd00::2]:443    ->  \0podnet-vnet/6/fd00::2/443
```

The IPv6 address is in the RFC 5952 form. The longest name is 60 bytes.

### 3.2 Interposed calls

| Call | Action on a virtual descriptor |
| --- | --- |
| `socket` | Make an `AF_UNIX` socket of the same type. Mark the descriptor as virtual. `SOCK_RAW` gives `EAFNOSUPPORT`. |
| `bind`, `connect` | Translate the address to the abstract name. |
| `sendto`, `recvfrom`, `sendmsg`, `recvmsg` | Translate the datagram addresses. |
| `accept`, `accept4` | The new descriptor is virtual. The logical peer is recorded. |
| `getsockname`, `getpeername` | Return the logical address. Truncate to `*len` as Linux does. A null address gives the length. A stream client with no `bind` gets a local address at `connect` (the shim address and a port of 49152-65535), and the server sees it as the peer. |
| `setsockopt`, `getsockopt` | Record `IPPROTO_TCP` options (`TCP_NODELAY`, `TCP_KEEPIDLE`) and answer them. |
| `close`, `dup`, `dup2`, `dup3`, `fcntl(F_DUPFD*)` | Clear or copy the virtual state. |

`read`, `write`, `poll`, `epoll` and `shutdown` are not interposed. They work
on the real `AF_UNIX` descriptor.

### 3.3 Limits

* The shim cannot reach a static binary. Use `podnet pod` or `podnet net proxy`
  for such programs.
* `recvmmsg` and `io_uring` are not interposed.
* `/proc/net/tcp`, `getifaddrs` and `/sys/class/net` do not show the virtual
  addresses.
* An abstract name is global on the host (in one network namespace). Two
  programs that bind the same virtual address and port get `EADDRINUSE`.
* An abstract name has no file permissions. Each user of the host can bind
  or connect to it. Thus the shim takes the same user only (`SO_PEERCRED`):
  `accept` closes a client of another user and takes the next client, and
  `connect` to a listener of another user fails with `ECONNREFUSED`. A
  datagram socket of the shim has `SO_PASSCRED`: before `recvfrom` and
  `recvmsg`, the shim drops each datagram of another user, with one line on
  stderr (T-075). `recv` and `read` are not interposed: a program that
  reads a datagram socket with them gets each datagram.

## 4. Stack

`NetStack::loopback()` makes a stack whose link sends each packet back into the
stack. Programs and the proxy on one host use it.

`NetStack::over_link(config)` makes a stack whose packets go to
`link_out()` and come from `link_in()`. A pump moves the packets between the
queues and a byte stream. `vnet::switch::pump` is that pump.

* The clock is `std::time::Instant`. The stack waits on the inbound queue or on
  the next timer of `smoltcp`. It does not spin.
* On a byte stream, each packet has a 2-byte big-endian length in front of it
  (`vnet::framing`).
* The MTU is 1280 or more.

## 5. Modes

### 5.1 Direct (one host, no stack)

Two programs with the shim talk through the abstract name. No other process is
necessary.

```text
program A: bind 10.66.0.2:8080     ->  \0podnet-vnet/4/10.66.0.2/8080
program B: connect 10.66.0.2:8080  ->  \0podnet-vnet/4/10.66.0.2/8080
```

### 5.2 Proxy

`podnet net proxy` puts a SOCKS5 and HTTP `CONNECT` front door on the stack.
`--forward VIRT=REAL` makes the stack listen on a virtual address and send each
connection to a real destination (`host:port` with a name or an address,
`[v6]:port`, or `unix:/path`). A target that is not loopback goes through the
proxy of the process, with `NO_PROXY`. A loopback target and a unix path go
direct. A failed dial logs the target, the way and the hop.

```sh
podnet net proxy --listen unix:/tmp/podnet-vnet.socks \
    --forward 10.66.0.2:8080=unix:/run/app.sock
```

A client must speak SOCKS5 over `AF_UNIX` itself, because `curl` does not
accept a unix-socket SOCKS proxy. On a host that permits a TCP bind, use
`--listen tcp://127.0.0.1:1080` and `ALL_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080`.

Each unix listener (`net proxy`, `net switch`, `net tailscale`) claims its
socket path first. A socket that another process serves gives exit 69. A file
that is not a socket gives exit 64. A stale socket is removed. A client that
sends no request in 30 s gets SOCKS5 code 4 or HTTP 504.

### 5.3 Switch (more than one host)

`podnet net switch` is a hub for stacks. Each stack connects to it with a byte
stream. The switch records the source address of each peer. It sends each
packet to the peer that owns the destination address, and it sends a packet
for an unknown address to all other peers.

* A source address is of the first peer that sends from it, until that peer
  disconnects. The switch drops a packet of another peer with that source
  address, and counts it.
* A unix listener takes the same user only (`SO_PEERCRED`).
* A TCP listener needs a shared token. Set `PODNET_SWITCH_TOKEN`, or give
  `--switch-token-file PATH` (the text of the file with no white space at
  the ends). With no token, `podnet net switch --listen tcp://...` exits 64.
  `podnet net proxy --switch tcp://...` sends the same token, from the same
  variable or its own `--switch-token-file`.
* The first line of a TCP peer is `podnet-switch/1 TOKEN` and a line feed.
  The switch answers `ok` and a line feed, then the frames start. A peer
  with a wrong first line gets `refused` and the switch closes it. A peer
  that sends no line in 10 s is closed. The token is not encrypted: on a
  network that others can see, use a tunnel (`podnet tunnel --forward`) or
  another encrypted path.

```sh
# Host S: the switch. Expose it with a tunnel when the hosts are far apart:
podnet net switch --listen unix:/tmp/sw.sock
podnet tunnel --forward unix:/tmp/sw.sock

# Host A: a stack at 10.66.0.2 with a service.
podnet connect wss://<host>/__podnet/ws -L unix:///tmp/sw.sock     # if remote
podnet net proxy --switch unix:/tmp/sw.sock --address 10.66.0.2 \
    --forward 10.66.0.2:8080=unix:/run/app.sock

# Host B: a stack at 10.66.0.3. Its proxy reaches 10.66.0.2:8080.
podnet net proxy --switch unix:/tmp/sw.sock --address 10.66.0.3 \
    --listen unix:/tmp/b.socks
```

Shim programs can also use the switch:

* `--control NAME` serves the control socket `\0NAME`. Start the program with
  `PODNET_VNET_CONTROL=NAME`. When the program binds a virtual address, the shim
  sends `RegisterBind`. The stack then listens on that address and sends each
  connection from the switch to the program.
* `--import VIRT` binds the abstract name of the remote address `VIRT` on this
  host. A shim program that connects to `VIRT` goes through the stack and the
  switch.
* These sockets take the same user only. The control socket has
  `SO_PASSCRED` and drops a datagram of another user. `--import` closes a
  client of another user. The stack does not send a connection to an
  abstract name that a process of another user holds. The unix listener of
  `podnet net switch` closes a peer of another user (also root).

### 5.4 Faults

`podnet net proxy --switch ... --address ...` takes `--drop`, `--duplicate` and
`--reorder` (probabilities from 0.0 to 1.0) and `--seed`. They put faults on
the packets that this stack sends to the switch; the switch itself
(`podnet net switch`) has no faults. The same seed gives the same faults. With
no `--switch`, the flags are a usage error (exit 64), as a value out of 0.0
to 1.0 is. In code, use `vnet::switch::Faults` and `FaultInjector`.

```sh
podnet net switch --listen unix:/tmp/sw.sock &
podnet net proxy --switch unix:/tmp/sw.sock --address 10.66.0.3 --drop 0.1 --seed 7
```

### 5.5 Routes to a SOCKS5 front door

A program can send a TCP connect to a SOCKS5 front door on a unix socket
(`podnet net tailscale`, `podnet net proxy`). There are three tiers:

| Tier | Shim | Destinations to the door | Other connects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tailnet (the default) | `libpodnet-socks.so` (`net socksify`) | `100.64.0.0/10` and `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48` | the real network |
| Chosen | `libpodnet-socks.so` (`net socksify --cidr ROUTE`) | only the listed routes | the real network |
| All | `libpodnet-socks.so` with `PODNET_SOCKS_ALL=1` | each TCP connect | none |

A route is `tailnet`, `ADDR`, `ADDR/BITS`, `IPV4:PORT` or `[IPV6]:PORT`.
`--cidr` is repeatable. The list replaces the tailnet default: add `tailnet`
to keep it. The shim keeps 32 routes at most. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address
matches as IPv4. With `--log` (`PODNET_SOCKS_LOG=1`), the shim logs each
route at the first connect, and each redirect.

```sh
eval "$(podnet net socksify --socket /tmp/podnet-socks.sock --cidr 127.0.0.1:3000 --cidr tailnet)"
```

The shim of the virtual network (`net shim`) takes the same routes with
`--socks-route ROUTE` and `--socks-socket PATH` (`PODNET_VNET_SOCKS` and
`PODNET_VNET_SOCKS_ROUTES`). A stream connect to a listed destination goes to
the door. Each other connect goes to its abstract name, as before.

```sh
podnet net shim --socks-route 192.168.1.5:5432 --socks-socket /tmp/podnet-socks.sock
```

podnet checks each route and exits 64 at a bad route. The C shims ignore a
bad route of the environment, and log it with the log variable.

## 6. Resolver, policy and capture

* `vnet::dns::Resolver` answers A and AAAA queries for a name table at
  `10.66.0.1:53`. `net proxy --map NAME=ADDR` and `--map-file PATH` fill the
  table of the gateway and of the proxy door; `net shim --map` and
  `--map-file` fill the table of `getaddrinfo`. An address outside the subnet
  is a usage error (exit 64). It can send unknown names to an upstream, or answer all
  unknown names with one address.
* `vnet::policy::Acl` has allow and deny rules for addresses and ports. The
  stack applies them when a program binds or connects.
* `vnet::record` writes the link packets to a pcap file. No `CAP_NET_RAW` is
  necessary. `Replayer` sends a capture into a stack again.

## 7. Control protocol

The shim sends control messages as datagrams to `\0<PODNET_VNET_CONTROL>`:

```text
u8 op | u16 length | payload
```

| Op | Message | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `RegisterBind` | `u32 id`, address |
| 2 | `RegisterConnect` | `u32 id`, address |
| 3 | `Unregister` | `u32 id` |
| 4 | `Datagram` | `u32 id`, from, to, data |

An address is `u8 family` (4 or 6), the address bytes and a `u16` port.
`ControlDecoder` finds the next frame after a bad frame and counts the dropped
bytes.

## 8. Verification

* `tests/af_inet_kernel.rs` reads the socket inode from `/proc/self/fd/N` and
  checks that the kernel lists the socket in `/proc/net/unix`, not in
  `/proc/net/tcp`. It does not use `getsockname`, because the shim answers that
  call.
* `tests/shim_no_socket.rs` checks programs that never open a socket.
* `vnet::switch` tests send 64 KiB through a switch with 10% drop, 5%
  duplicates and 5% reorder, and check that the bytes arrive in order.

<!-- document: docs/target-environment.md -->

# Target environment

podnet is for Linux hosts with strong network limits. This document gives the
hosts that were measured, the other host conditions that podnet must handle,
and the rules of podnet for them.

Each fact has a date and a mark:

* **measured**: a command ran on the host, and the result is given.
* **inferred**: the fact comes from the code or from documents, not from a run.

## Limits and the parts of podnet for them

| Limit on the host | Part of `podnet` | Tested |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No UDP to the edge | HTTP/2 edge leg on TCP 7844 | CI, live against the Cloudflare edge |
| Only TCP 443 out | QUIC edge leg inside WARP (MASQUE) | CI, live |
| No DNS resolver | DNS over HTTPS by IP address (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8), then a static edge list | CI and a sandbox with an HTTP proxy |
| Egress through a proxy only | HTTP `CONNECT`, SOCKS5 and `NO_PROXY` for each connection | `tests/egress.rs` |
| No root, no TUN, no network namespace | `podnet pod` (seccomp backend), `podnet warp run` | CI and a sandbox |
| No `AF_INET` bind | `podnet net` (shim and userspace stack), unix-socket origins | CI and a sandbox |

The live workflow (`.github/workflows/live.yml`, on each push and each day) runs `podnet demo` with each
edge leg on a GitHub runner and fetches the public URL. One limit stays: a proxy that terminates TLS cannot
carry the edge connection or the MASQUE connection, because both need the Cloudflare certificate chain
(and MASQUE needs a client certificate).

## Measured hosts

### A sandbox with an egress proxy (2026-11-01)

The tools: `podnet status`, `podnet doctor`, `podnet pod doctor --json`, `podnet net doctor`,
`openssl s_client -proxy`, `curl`, `podnet demo`.

| Fact | Result | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Egress | One HTTP `CONNECT` proxy, named in `HTTPS_PROXY` | measured |
| TLS roots | `SSL_CERT_FILE` names a private bundle (123 roots) | measured |
| TLS to `api.trycloudflare.com` through the proxy | The real chain (Google Trust Services). The proxy does not re-terminate TLS for this name. | measured |
| `CONNECT` to an IP address (`1.1.1.1:443`) | The proxy resets the connection | measured |
| `CONNECT` to `cloudflare-dns.com:443` | Works (HTTP 200 from DoH) | measured |
| `CONNECT` to the edge (`198.41.200.x:7844`) | The proxy resets the connection | measured |
| `podnet doctor` (2026-11-01): `CONNECT` to the edge on 7844 (name and address) and to MASQUE `162.159.198.2:443` | The proxy answers 200, then no TLS byte comes back: "the proxy answers and carries nothing". `api.trycloudflare.com` (Google Trust Services) and `api.cloudflareclient.com` (Let's Encrypt) have valid chains. 0 of 3 legs can work. | measured |
| QUIC on UDP 7844, no proxy | No answer (the handshake times out); `podnet net doctor`: `UDP egress ... ? unknown` | measured |
| `listen(2)` after `bind(2)` (AF_INET, AF_UNIX) | Allowed (`SO_ACCEPTCONN=1`) | measured |
| DNS on UDP 53 to `1.1.1.1` | An answer | measured |
| `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)` | Allowed | measured |
| `bind(AF_INET6, [::1]:0)` | `EAFNOSUPPORT` | measured |
| `/dev/net/tun` | Present | measured |
| `seccomp(SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF)` | A listener installs | measured |

The effect: a quick tunnel cannot reach the edge from this host. Edge
discovery works through the proxy with DNS over HTTPS by name, because the
proxy refuses DoH by IP address. The test suite of podnet runs here.

### A GitHub runner, ubuntu-24.04 (2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01)

The tools: `.github/workflows/live.yml` (run 41260604779), `release.yml`
(`release-short.sh`).

| Fact | Result | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QUIC on UDP 7844 | Registers | measured |
| HTTP/2 on TCP 7844 | Registers | measured |
| QUIC inside WARP MASQUE on TCP 443 | Registers | measured |
| UDP 7844 dropped (`iptables DROP`) | `--protocol auto` registers over HTTP/2 after 2.4 s (the 2 s stagger) | measured |
| UDP and TCP 7844 dropped | `--protocol auto` registers over `quic+warp` after 6.7 s (two 2 s staggers and the WARP setup) | measured |
| UDP and TCP 7844 dropped, `--transport relay` | `http2+relay` registers through `tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev` in 0.74 s (ord02); the public URL answers 200 (run 41303368779) | measured |
| No system resolver | Names come from DoH by IP address at `1.1.1.1` | measured |
| No system resolver, `1.1.1.1` and `1.0.0.1` blocked | Names come from DoH by IP address at Google (`8.8.8.8`) | measured |
| A local `CONNECT` proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY` | DoH by IP (`1.1.1.1:443`), the API, the HTTP/2 edge leg (`:7844`) and the fetch of the public URL go through it; no QUIC is tried | measured |
| Unprivileged user namespaces | AppArmor limits them: a namespace can be made, but `lo` cannot come up | measured |
| `podnet warp run --backend seccomp` | Works (`warp=on`) | measured |

### An IPv6-only host (the IPv6-only kit, 2026-11-02; a runner)

The kit ran in a netns and in a VM with IPv6 only (NAT66 out through
WARP). `scripts/v6only/` makes the same host on a runner: the namespace
`v6up` has IPv4 and `podnet warp tun --default-route`; `v6only` behind it
has IPv6 only (no IPv4 route; the address 127.0.0.1 stays). The step "An IPv6-only host" of `live.yml` runs
`scripts/v6only/acceptance.sh`.

| Fact | Result | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A connect to an IPv4 address | `ENETUNREACH` | measured (kit) |
| `podnet warp run` | IPv4 and UDP for the program through WARP; a tunnel at 1.9 to 2.2 MB/s | measured (kit) |
| A tunnel with TCP 443 and DNS only | Ready in 13 s; after `kill -9`, the supervisor starts it again in less than 30 s, with a new URL | measured (kit) |

### The test box (a GitHub runner, from 2026-11-01)

`scripts/test_in_box.sh` copies the sandbox above onto a runner, with no
Podman box: `iptables -m owner` lets the user `podnetbox` reach only
`scripts/box/proxy.py` (names on 443, the MASQUE address, the refusal
texts of the sandbox) and a fault stand-in. No UDP, no direct TCP, no
DNS, no IPv6. `scripts/box/probe.py` checks the box against
`scripts/box/report.txt` first, and a proxy that allows each target must
fail that check. The steps:

| Step | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `podnet --version` | runs (a binary that exits 3 makes the box exit 1) |
| probe, then a planted wrong policy | the box matches; the planted policy fails |
| `podnet doctor` | `quic` and `http2` refused, `quic+warp` ok |
| `demo --transport direct` (negative control) | fails |
| `demo` | registers on `quic+warp` through the proxy, and the URL answers |
| `demo` with the MASQUE address refused (negative control) | fails |
| an edge that accepts and says nothing | the HTTP/2 leg fails in its limit, no hang |

`.github/workflows/live.yml` runs it on each push and each day.

## Other host conditions

| Condition | What podnet does | Mark | Code or test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HOME` is not set | The state directory is `podnet-<uid>` in the temporary directory, never the current directory | measured (test) | `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs`; `tests/cli/startup.rs` `an_empty_environment_works` |
| The uid has no passwd entry | podnet reads the home from `HOME` only and does not call `getpwuid`. A client (`ssh`, `git`) fails, and `ssh-keygen` exits 0 and writes no key. `podnet net doctor` shows it (`passwd entry for this uid`). `podnet net passwd-shim` gives the preload `fakepwd.so` and `SANDHOME_PASSWD` for each client | inferred; the probe and the shim: measured (test) | `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs`; `crates/podnet-vnet/src/tailscale_ssh.rs`; `crates/podnet-vnet/src/doctor.rs` `passwd_probe_names_the_shim`; `tests/cli/net.rs` `passwd_shim_prints_the_preload` |
| The temporary directory is `noexec` | A shim goes to the first directory that is writable and not `noexec` | inferred | `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs` `exec_dir` |
| A shim directory in `/tmp` exists already (another user made it) | podnet uses the directory only when it belongs to this user, is not a symlink, and other users cannot write it; else it tries the next directory. A cached library is used only when it is a file of this user that other users cannot write | measured (test) | `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs` `exec_dir_refuses_a_directory_open_to_others`; `crates/podnet-vnet/src/shim.rs` `a_planted_library_is_not_used_from_the_cache` |
| The state directory is read-only | podnet tries the next directory of the chain; a WARP registration does not start when no directory can be written | measured (test) | `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs`; `src/warp/mod.rs` `register_or_load` |
| The proxy re-terminates TLS | Give its root with `--ca-file` or `SSL_CERT_FILE` for the API and DoH. The edge and MASQUE cannot pass through it: they need the Cloudflare chain, and MASQUE needs a client certificate | inferred | `crates/podnet-core/src/trust.rs`; `tests/tls.rs` |
| The proxy refuses `CONNECT` to an IP address | DoH by name (`cloudflare-dns.com`, `dns.google`, `dns.google.com`) through the proxy | measured | `src/resolve.rs` `settings` (`pod_dns::Names::Last`) |
| The proxy answers 407 | The error names each scheme of `Proxy-Authenticate`; podnet answers Basic and Digest (MD5, MD5-sess, SHA-256, SHA-256-sess), and the advice follows what it sent | measured (test) | `PodUtils/podcrates:crates/pod-proxy/src/proxy_auth.rs` `a_407_names_the_schemes`, `a_407_with_digest_does_not_say_basic_only`; `tests/egress.rs` `a_407_names_the_schemes` |
| No `/proc` | The seccomp backend of `podnet pod` cannot read the memory of the program; `podnet pod doctor` reports it | inferred | `crates/podnet-netns/src/seccomp/mem.rs` |
| `/proc/<pid>/mem` and `process_vm_writev` are refused | `getsockname` and `getpeername` answer `EOPNOTSUPP` under the seccomp backend; QUIC clients fail, and a program that reads its own address can crash (a Go `LocalAddr()` type assertion). A warning and the `write program memory` row of `pod doctor` say so; `--backend netns` avoids it | measured (issue 186) | `crates/podnet-netns/src/sockopt.rs` `handle_sockname`; `tests/pod_seccomp/tcp.rs` `getpeername_is_the_inet_address_or_eopnotsupp` |
| The clock is wrong | A certificate error gives the clock of the host | measured (test) | `tests/tls.rs` `an_expired_certificate_names_the_host_clock` |
| `bind` is allowed and `listen` is refused | `podnet net doctor` gives `listen(...) FAIL`; `warp proxy`, `connect -L`, `net proxy`, `net switch`, `net tailscale` and `relay connect --listen` need a listener (`net proxy`, `net switch` and `net tailscale` default to a unix path) | measured (test) | `crates/podnet-vnet/src/doctor.rs`; `tests/cli/startup.rs` `doctor_tells_listen_from_bind` |
| Outbound UDP is refused (EPERM, ICMP) | `--protocol auto` does not try QUIC on UDP 7844 | measured (test) | `crates/podnet-core/src/udp.rs`; `tunnel::plan_with_udp` |
| No IPv6 (`EAFNOSUPPORT`) | Direct dials alternate the families and go on to the next address after 250 ms | inferred | `PodUtils/podcrates:crates/pod-proxy/src/race.rs` `dial_addrs` |

## Other networks to the front door

podnet has no built-in Tor or Psiphon client. Each of these networks gives a
local SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, and `--proxy` sends the connections of podnet
(the WARP API and the MASQUE session) through it. The WARP traffic then
leaves the other network at its exit, and the front door sees that exit.

* Tor (issue 159). Start `tor`; it listens on SOCKS5 127.0.0.1:9050.

  ```sh
  podnet --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050 warp register
  podnet --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050 warp proxy
  ```

  The API can refuse a Tor exit. Then register with no proxy, and use
  `--proxy` for the session only (`warp proxy` loads the saved device).
  `--no-relay` keeps the session on Tor: the WebSocket relay is a second
  path that does not use Tor.
* Psiphon (issue 158). The console client of psiphon-tunnel-core gives a
  SOCKS5 port and an HTTP port (`LocalSocksProxyPort` and
  `LocalHttpProxyPort` of its config).

  ```sh
  podnet --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:PORT warp --no-relay proxy
  ```

* A command as the carrier: `--proxy 'http+exec:COMMAND'` runs COMMAND for
  each connection and speaks HTTP `CONNECT` on its stdin and stdout, as the
  `ProxyCommand` of SSH.
* A nested session (issue 156): a second device whose session goes through
  the first. The front door of the second device sees the exit of the
  first.

  ```sh
  podnet warp --identity a.json proxy --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:40000 &
  podnet --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:40000 warp --identity b.json proxy \
      --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:40001
  ```

  The clients of 40001 use the second device. Each packet is in two
  sessions, so the MTU and the speed are lower.

`scripts/live-batch2.sh` (in `.github/workflows/live.yml`) checks the nested
session.

## Rules of podnet

1. Use one egress path for each connection: the proxy of `--proxy` or the
   variables, with `NO_PROXY`. Code: `src/egress.rs`, over `pod-proxy`. Followed by each
   command; `podnet pod` has its own upstream list (`podnet pod -x`).
2. Do not send UDP around a proxy. Code: `tunnel::plan_with_proxy`.
3. Resolve names with a chain that works with no system resolver. Code:
   `src/resolve.rs`.
4. Check each TLS certificate; take extra roots only from the user. Code:
   `crates/podnet-core/src/trust.rs`.
5. Write no file in the current directory unless the user names it; keep
   secrets in private files. Code: `crates/podnet-core/src/state.rs`, `src/warp/mod.rs`.
6. Say which hop failed. Code: `crates/podnet-core/src/hop.rs`.
7. Start the next edge leg after a short stagger, not after a full time
   limit. Code: `crates/podnet-core/src/race.rs`.

The doctors (`podnet doctor`, `podnet net doctor`, `podnet pod doctor`) measure a host. Give
their output in an issue, with `podnet status`.
